articles.title: Mike Tomlin is a Super Bowl-winning coach. His real passion might have been ‘Minecraft.’
articles.summary: As the coach of one of the NFL’s most successful franchises, the Pittsburgh Steelers, for nearly two decades, Mike Tomlin was charged with building championship-caliber teams.
articles.body: As the coach of one of the NFL’s most successful franchises, the Pittsburgh Steelers, for nearly two decades, Mike Tomlin was charged with building championship-caliber teams. In his free time, Tomlin was building something different: an elaborate cityscape in the video game “Minecraft.” On his YouTube channel on Wednesday, Tomlin revealed part of that map, which he said he had been working on for more than 12 years. Within four hours, the episode had been viewed more than 334,000 times. By the next morning, that total had doubled. “I’ve always had an interest in architecture and so forth,” Tomlin said in the video, which has amassed over 900,000 views. “And so I started building this creative city.” Tomlin may have been perfecting the map for more than a decade, but his hobby had only become public three weeks earlier. The 54-year-old stepped down as the Steelers’ coach in January after 19 consecutive winning seasons, which included a Super Bowl victory. As his debut season as a broadcaster for NBC’s “Sunday Night Football” began last month, Tomlin revealed in an interview with Craig Melvin that his passions, in fact, ranged beyond football. Watching his then-young children spend hours playing “Minecraft” had inspired him to see what all the fuss was about. As they became teenagers and went off to college, their interest waned. Not Tomlin’s, though. “More than anything, it was therapeutic for me,” Tomlin said. “So, mindless entertainment. I’m not a big TV watcher. It allowed me to detach from the realities and the pressures of life.” With the Steelers, Tomlin was known for unique sayings referred to as “Tomlinisms.” In 2020, he famously wouldn’t allow Covid restrictions to be used as a hardship, saying, “We do not care.” So it stunned some football fans last month to hear that what Tomlin privately did care so much for was a video game that is immensely popular with elementary-age kids. Since its creation in 2009, “Minecraft” has become the bestselling game of all time, with more than 300 million copies sold, Microsoft said in 2024, and has since spawned a popular movie. An open-world “sandbox” game, “Minecraft” allows users to build whatever their creativity desires using a variety of materials, from different types of stone and wood to beyond. Some players build fantasy worlds where building physics don’t apply. Players often build in multiple maps. Tomlin stuck to just one, however, preferring to build what appears to be a midsize city centered around bodies of water and with a dense urban core that includes sports stadiums, high-rises and a PNC Bank. The map showed hills and wooded suburbs. In other words, not all that dissimilar to … Pittsburgh. Narrating his tour with a matter-of-fact delivery not out of place from his past weekly news conferences, Tomlin used verbiage a real estate developer would approve of while saying that his map all began by creating a bay. Then he built a boutique hotel, complete with an executive spa, therapy rooms and an “appropriate number of public restrooms.” Showing off a glass ceiling over the hotel’s conference room, Tomlin called his design philosophy “lighting-conscious.” Some commenters online questioned how much time Tomlin had spent building while also working in the NFL, an industry known for its workaholic culture. Former Steelers running back Le’Veon Bell wrote, “we were tryna win super bowls and coach T was on minecraft building cities 😭.” More so, the reaction tended to center on Tomlin’s dedication to realism. “Never thought I’d watch Mike Tomlin discuss lighting and basement speakeasies,” one YouTube commenter said. On a Reddit thread devoted to Tomlin’s build, one person wrote, “When Mike Tomlin first mentioned this whole thing, I was NOT expecting such an impressive city!” Tomlin built buildings by themes, intentionally placing them next to rivers, bays and lakes he carved out of the map. His designs are intricate; residential buildings included different floor plans for the penthouse than the lower floors. Kitchens featured islands. Bathrooms featured plants. Bedrooms included paintings. The living spaces in one high-rise, which was down the street from buildings named “CVS” and “7-Eleven,” wrapped around a central aquarium. Nearby were stadiums for professional soccer and baseball. At some point, Tomlin acknowledged becoming “obsessed with rooftop penthouses” with great views. That focus then spilled over into designing spaces for indoor and outdoor entertainment, balconies, home offices, and his-and-hers bathroom concepts. “Find someone who loves you like Coach Tomlin loves a Jack & Jill bathroom,” another YouTube commenter said. It was one of many jokes sparked by Tomlin’s “Minecraft” devotion. Yet, perhaps it shouldn’t have been all that surprising. In “Minecraft,” Tomlin seems to have found similarities to the mixture of creativity and discipline required in the world of the NFL. Coaches’ lives abide by a rigid structure of practices, games and the offseason calendar. They conceive exotic play designs and defensive coverages, then put them into practice by obsessing over details and precision. “Football is an emotional game played by high-energy men who are really emotional,” Tomlin said in 2022. “They need to hear a steady voice. They need to hear consistency in messaging in belief, and so it’s my job to exemplify that.” Tomlin was praised as a coach for his never-too-high, never-too-low personality. The kind of person whose idea of winding down after a long day in the spotlight might include ensuring his “Minecraft” map had a “certain density,” as he said. When Tomlin dropped his son Dino off at college, he said he was inspired to re-create the look of off-campus housing into his own city. “Bro I used to come home sometimes and my PlayStation would just be gone,” one of Tomlin’s sons, Mason, posted on X. “And I wasn’t in trouble.” At one point during Tomlin’s tour, he focused on a tall, beige building labeled “Trump Tower.” “Not an endorsement,” a chyron said on the video. “This build is (circa) 2015… We didn’t think he would win. Twice.” Its penthouse had an “unbelievable open floor plan,” Tomlin said approvingly. He promised his roughly 76,000 YouTube subscribers more episodes. “I’ll give you a tour of this aquarium at some point,” he said. “It’s crazy.”

articles.title: In 1998, a wide receiver the NFL had blacklisted in the draft fell to the 21st pick; 1 season later, he had rewritten every receiving record a rookie had ever touched and the league was quietly terrified
articles.summary: Randy Moss waited. Twenty teams passed on the Marshall receiver in the 1998 NFL draft, most of them worried about his past, not his hands.
articles.body: Randy Moss waited. Twenty teams passed on the Marshall receiver in the 1998 NFL draft, most of them worried about his past, not his hands. Minnesota took him at No. 21. Within months he was a problem defenses could not solve. Moss caught 69 passes for 1,313 yards and 17 touchdowns, a rookie record for touchdown catches that still stands. He made the Pro Bowl, won Offensive Rookie of the Year, and helped a 15-1 team. The sharpest part of the story is not the slide. It is how little the league understood what it was ignoring.Why Randy Moss fell to No. 21 in the 1998 NFL DraftTalent was never the question. Moss had scored more than 50 touchdowns in two seasons at Marshall, and every scout knew it. The question was his record away from the field. As a teenager in West Virginia he was convicted of battery after a fight at his high school, spent time in jail and lost a scholarship offer from Notre Dame. Florida State signed him, then dismissed him after a positive marijuana test violated his probation. Marshall gave him a third start.Draft rooms are cautious places. A receiver who runs like Moss but carries that file makes general managers nervous, and they remember the picks that blow up. Some teams reportedly took him off their boards entirely. So he sat while the names kept coming. Twenty were called before his, including Ryan Leaf, Andre Wadsworth and Curtis Enis, none of whom came close to his career.Why Minnesota Vikings took the riskThe Vikings were not a desperate team. They had gone 9-7 the year before, with Dennis Green running the sideline and Cris Carter owning one side of the field. Randall Cunningham took over at quarterback early that season. Carter had his own rough chapter, released by Philadelphia in 1990 over substance problems, and he knew what a second chance felt like. Moss would not have to carry the offense or be the loudest voice in the room.It was a smart fit more than a gamble. Defenses already had to worry about Carter, which meant Moss often saw single coverage. Put a deep threat in that spot and the math changes fast.What Randy Moss actually did as a rookieHe started fast and never really slowed. His 69 catches went for 1,313 yards, an average of 19.0 per grab. His 17 touchdowns led the league and remain the most ever by a rookie. Minnesota finished 15-1 and scored 556 points, the most in NFL history at that point.Part of the damage came from how he played. Moss had long, gliding strides that made corners think they were fine until the ball was already in the air. He tracked deep throws better than most receivers with twice his experience, and he caught contested balls like they were gifts.His loudest day came on Thanksgiving in Dallas, a team that had passed on him. He caught three touchdowns, finished with 163 yards and the Vikings won. Cowboys fans got a close look at what they had skipped.The season ended badly. Atlanta beat Minnesota in overtime in the NFC title game after Gary Anderson, perfect on field goals all year, missed a late kick. Moss deserved a Super Bowl shot that year and never got one.Did Randy Moss really rewrite every rookie record?Not quite, and it is worth correcting because the real story holds up on its own. The touchdown mark still stands. The yardage mark did not last. Anquan Boldin, Justin Jefferson and Ja'Marr Chase have all passed 1,313 yards as rookies, and Chase reached 1,455 in 2021. Moss no longer sits near the top of that list.As for the league being terrified, regret is closer to the truth. Teams had every chance to take him and chose not to. After his first season, they could not unsee what they had missed. Defensive coordinators spent the next decade building coverage plans around him, and few found a reliable answer.What the Randy Moss slide still teaches scoutsHis fall is now a standard case study in how teams weigh character against production. The cost of passing is easy to measure in hindsight. Moss retired with 156 receiving touchdowns, set the single-season record with 23 for New England in 2007, and earned a Hall of Fame place in 2018.The useful lesson is narrower than a slogan. A bad file is information, not a verdict. Teams that ask what surrounds a player, such as veteran leaders, a clear role and a steady coach, tend to decide better than teams that just count red flags. Minnesota did that homework. articles.title: Travis Etienne Jr. Injured, Latest News on Saints RB's Status, Timeline and Fantasy Implications
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints will be without their starting running back for several weeks.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints will be without their starting running back for several weeks.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Travis Etienne Jr. will be placed on the injured reserve after suffering a hamstring injury, meaning he'll have to miss at least four games.

Etienne, who is in his first season with New Orleans, went to the locker room halfway through the third quarter of Sunday's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders and did not return.

After a career season with the Jacksonville Jaguars a year ago, Etienne has gotten off to a bit of a slow start, recording 128 rushing yards on 30 carries through the first three games.

Etienne's absence over the next few weeks means Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller should see an increase in touches for the time being. Kamara has rushed for 51 yards on 18 carries this year, while Miller has 44 yards on 13 carries. Neither running back has found the end zone yet.

For fantasy managers looking for a replacement for Etienne, Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon and New York Jets running back Braelon Allen jump out as possible candidates.

Dolphins' starting running back De'Von Achane landed on the injured reserve this week and Jaylen Wright is questionable heading into Week 4, so Gordon should get the bulk of the carries.

The Jets are likely to be without Breece Hall this week, and Allen is the first up behind him.

All things considered, the Saints have had a decent start to the year. After taking the Detroit Lions to overtime in Week 1, they upset the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2. They're coming off a one-score loss to the Raiders and have a manageable game against the Atlanta Falcons on deck.

Still, losing Etienne will make things a bit more difficult.

articles.title: "I guess I'm a little sick": Josh Allen opens up on his knee injury concerns ahead of Week 4 clash against the New England Patriots
articles.summary: Josh Allen, the Buffalo Bills’ star player, has always bounced back on the field in the last few years even as he sustained brutal injuries on the field.
articles.body: Josh Allen, the Buffalo Bills’ star player, has always bounced back on the field in the last few years even as he sustained brutal injuries on the field. Despite his record breaking performance in the last few seasons, the Buffalo Bills have missed out on winning the Super Bowl. While the team has recorded a winning streak in the new season so far, at the Week 3 clash against the Los Angeles Chargers, there have been some concerns about Josh Allen’s knee.Josh Allen reflects on his injury as he gears up to face the New England Patriots in Week 4A few hours ago, the 4 time Pro Bowler Josh Alen spoke to reporters about injury concerns as he said, "I guess I'm a little sick because I do love this game…”The Buffalo Bills’ top quarterback added, “I love everything about it. I do enjoy waking up on a Tuesday feeling extremely sore, especially after a win. It means that you did what you could do and found a way to win a football game. You're always going to feel more sore after the losses. articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. Injury Update, Latest News on Cowboys CB's Status After Steelers Trade
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who arrived in town after the Pittsburgh Steelers traded him on Wednesday, hopes he'll be able to make his debut Sunday at the Houston Texans as he continues to work his way onto the field from a back injury.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who arrived in town after the Pittsburgh Steelers traded him on Wednesday, hopes he'll be able to make his debut Sunday at the Houston Texans as he continues to work his way onto the field from a back injury .

"We're just trying to take things day by day, and if everything looks good, then we should be out there," Porter said following his first Cowboys practice on Thursday, per ESPN's Todd Archer .

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer expressed optimism about Porter's chances, via Archer.

"We'd like him to play, but we'll see how the week goes. I think he's excited about the opportunity to maybe play, but we'll see how the rest of the week goes. But it was a good start today," Schottenheimer said.

Porter, a former Penn State star, was the No. 32 overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft. He played his first three seasons with the Steelers, amassing 165 tackles (120 solo), 31 pass breakups and three interceptions over 47 games (41 starts).

Last year, opposing quarterbacks only completed 32-of-66 passes in his direction en route to a paltry 57.2 QB rating, per Pro Football Reference .

Porter entered this season on the final year of his rookie contract, and he and the Steelers worked toward a contract extension. However, one never materialized, leading to a months-long standoff.

Archer and ESPN's Brooke Pryor provided more information on Porter, who did not participate in any offseason activities leading into the regular season.

"The heart of the dispute was the guaranteed money within the contract's structure, sources told ESPN, and the sides never made meaningful progress on agreeing to terms despite talks as late as hours before kickoff of the Steelers' Week 1 game against the Atlanta Falcons. The Steelers then stopped talks because they don't negotiate during the regular season as a longstanding organizational principle."

Porter hasn't played in the Steelers' first three games as he deals with the aforementioned back issue plus conditioning concerns. He gave some insight to reporters (h/t Pryor) about the matter on Wednesday.

"It's both," Porter said. "My back has its moments where [there's] a flare-up here and there, and we're still just trying to get my conditioning down to just me being out there as much as possible."

The Steelers soon traded Porter to Dallas for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder. Now he'll joins a pass defense that can use his services. The Cowboys have allowed the sixth-most passing yards per attempt ( 7.2 ) in the NFL. They've also given up seven passing touchdowns and no interceptions thus far.

We'll soon find out if Porter makes his debut. Kickoff in Houston is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

articles.title: Dak Prescott Hypes Joey Porter Jr.'s Trade to Cowboys from Steelers, CB Can 'Shut a Side Down'
articles.summary: Dak Prescott was excited about the Dallas Cowboys acquiring cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
Dak Prescott was excited about the Dallas Cowboys acquiring cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday night.

"He's a good corner," Prescott said Thursday, per ESPN's Todd Archer . "He's the guy that can play physical, play man to man and take a receiver away, shut a side down. And now to have that on our side, playmaker when the ball's in the air. I know he went and got one on me on almost a 50-50 ball that he didn't make it seem that way at all. And when you've got a guy like that with ball skills and hunger for the ball, you want him on your team. I'm so glad we have him."

The Steelers sent Porter to Dallas in exchange for a 2027 conditional sixth-round draft pick as well as a 2028 second-round pick. He needs to be on the Cowboys' gameday roster for two contests this year in order for the 2027 pick to go through.

Porter's change of scenery came after he was unsuccessful in his attempt to land a new contract from the Steelers heading into the 2026 season. He eventually missed Pittsburgh's first three games of the year while dealing with back issues .

The former second-round pick operated as key piece of the Steelers' secondary from 2023-25, starting in 41 of his 47 games played across that span.

Last season, Porter racked up 52 tackles and one interception to go along with one sack in 14 games. His 14 passes defended ranked No. 12 among all players.

Porter has found success against Prescott in the past, picking him off during a matchup between the Cowboys and Steelers in Week 5 of the 2024 season.

Dallas only sits at 1-2 to open its 2026 campaign, although Prescott has still been largely efficient in the pocket.

He's completed 69.5 percent of his throws for 730 yards and seven touchdowns compared to one interception. Prescott's 80.0 QBR ranks No. 5 among 30 qualified quarterbacks this season, via ESPN .

As the Cowboys look to put their slow start behind them, expectations are high for Porter.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers says there is "zero debate" about retiring, yet his final Thursday night game feels like unfinished business
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers will play the last scheduled Thursday night game of his career when the Pittsburgh Steelers visit the Cleveland Browns at 8:15 p.m.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers will play the last scheduled Thursday night game of his career when the Pittsburgh Steelers visit the Cleveland Browns at 8:15 p.m. ET on Amazon Prime. He sits one win short of tying Tom Brady's record of 14 Thursday wins by a quarterback. Both teams are 2-1. The Steelers beat Cincinnati 30-27 last week, and the Browns edged Carolina 21-18. Pittsburgh also arrives with an 0-9 mark in Thursday road games against AFC North opponents. Rodgers, 42, plans to retire after this 22nd season, so Cleveland is his final shot at matching Brady's number.Is Aaron Rodgers really retiring after the 2026 season?Everything he has said points to yes. Rodgers signed a one-year deal with Pittsburgh in May after more than four months of deliberating. Asked whether this would be his last season, he told reporters, “Yes, this is it.” When he returned to training camp on July 28, a reporter asked if he was weighing another year after this one. His answer was short. “No. Zero debate.”That certainty changes how Thursday reads. Rodgers turns 43 in December, and this is his last scheduled Thursday game. Brady's mark is 14, so a win ties it and nothing more. There is no later date to push past him. Rodgers has 46 touchdowns and seven interceptions on Thursdays. Against Cleveland, he has thrown 11 touchdowns without an interception in five games.He does not sound sentimental about the night itself. “I just suck it up for those three hours and then know you get a reward on the back end. I think it’s part of the game now because of the money that’s in it. I think I’m just excited about the weekend,” Rodgers said. If the Brady record matters to him, he is keeping it quiet.Can the Steelers beat the Browns on a short week?History says be careful. Pittsburgh has lost all nine Thursday road games against AFC North teams, and four of those came against Cleveland. The Browns won 24-19 in a snowstorm two years ago. The 2019 meeting is remembered for Myles Garrett ripping off Mason Rudolph's helmet and hitting him with it. Cleveland has also won seven straight Thursday games, tied for the fourth-longest streak in NFL history.Defensive tackle Cam Heyward does not see the short week as a one-sided problem. “But the great thing about it is they got to deal with the same problems we are. So it’s an even playing field,” he said.The Steelers have roster questions, though. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. went to Dallas late Wednesday for two draft picks after a contract impasse, and Jalen Ramsey is questionable with a broken wrist. Jaylen Warren should carry the load again after a career-high 176 total yards against Cincinnati, since Rico Dowdle is out with a toe injury.The line play may decide it. Browns tackles have allowed a 13.5% pressure rate, second highest in the league, and Tytus Howard's 17 pressures are tied for the most by a right tackle. TJ Watt has 17.5 sacks in 15 games against Cleveland. Deshaun Watson has lost all three starts against Pittsburgh and been sacked 18 times. articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. Says Steelers 'Disrespected' Him in Contract Talks Before Cowboys Trade
articles.summary: Before being traded to the Dallas Cowboys on Wednesday, Joey Porter Jr. was engaged in contract talks with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
Before being traded to the Dallas Cowboys on Wednesday, Joey Porter Jr. was engaged in contract talks with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

In his eyes, he was being "disrespected" by the Steelers.

"It was a hard process, a lot of ups and downs," Porter told reporters on Thursday. "Definitely felt disrespected. Definitely felt undervalued. But that's old news now. That's how I look at it. I'm on to new beginnings, new chapters."

With his new team, Porter already feels like he's being valued more than he was in Pittsburgh.

"It was the value. I didn't feel like it was really that over there," Porter told reporters . "[Dallas] is showing me that they value me more over here. That's really all I need to show what I can do."

Porter is currently in the final year of his rookie deal and has a base salary of $3.052 million this season. per Spotrac, he has a market value of $27.4 million per year, which would make him the fifth-highest-paid cornerback in the NFL.

While Porter feels more valued in Dallas, the Cowboys don't plan to sign him to an extension during the regular season, according to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz .

The Steelers tried to extend Porter over the offseason but couldn't reach an agreement before the season started. General manager Omar Khan said in August that the team didn't plan to negotiate a deal during the regular season.

Porter has not yet played this season, but he's coming off a year in which he recorded 52 tackles, 14 passes defensed, a sack and an interception while playing 94 percent of the Steelers' defensive snaps.

He allowed the third-fewest yards per coverage snap last season, only behind Las Vegas' Erick Sokes and Denver's Pat Surtain II.

Dallas spent the offseason bolstering its defense, but the Cowboys have still allowed the third-most yards per game (387.0) and the eighth-most points per game (27.3) through the first three games.

Clearly, Dallas needs more on defense, and Porter will look to provide it.

The Cowboys take on the Houston Texans on Sunday, and ESPN's Adam Schefter noted that there's "a chance" Porter will be available.

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. says he felt 'disrespected' and 'undervalued' by Steelers, wants to finish his career with Cowboys
articles.summary: The fourth-year cornerback was traded to Dallas on Wednesday after missing all of training camp, the preseason and first three games of the season with a bac...
articles.body:
Following Wednesday's trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers to the Dallas Cowboys, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. said the back injury that sidelined him through all of training camp, the preseason and the first three games of the regular season is "feeling better."

The fourth-year pro was ruled out for the Steelers' Thursday night matchup versus the Cleveland Browns to open Week 4. Yet Porter could be available for the Cowboys on Sunday versus the Houston Texans after being acquired for a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-rounder, according to ESPN .

"He moved around good today," Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters after Thursday's practice, via The Athletic . "It was a good start today. It was a positive first day."

Porter was not listed on the Cowboys' injury report for Thursday.

That would be an impressive recovery for Porter, whose injury status many attributed to him holding out for a new contract from the Steelers. Taking the field promptly after being traded to the Cowboys does little to dispel that notion.

Porter himself lent credence to the skepticism with his remarks about his experience in Pittsburgh to reporters on Thursday, saying he didn't feel valued.

"Definitely felt disrespected, definitely felt undervalued," Porter said, via the Cowboys' official website . "But that's old news now. That's how I look at it. I'm onto new beginnings, new chapters. I'm a Cowboy, I'm in Dallas, so I'm happy about that."

He laughed when it was pointed out that his back felt fine in Dallas.

Porter and the Cowboys still need to work out a new contract, which was the basis of his issues with the Steelers. Reportedly, he is seeking a deal that pays him a $30 million average annual salary , which would put him among the top six cornerbacks in the NFL, according to Over the Cap .

However, Porter appears to be assured that a new deal will be coming. He made it clear that he wants to continue playing in Dallas.

"I'm down with it if they are," he said, via The Athletic's Jon Machota . "I want to finish my career here."

Last season Porter Jr. played in 14 games for Pittsburgh, totaling 52 tackles and 14 passes defended with one interception. The Steelers' 2023 second-round selection (No. 32 overall) out of Penn State has three career interceptions in 47 games during his three NFL seasons.

articles.title: Le'Veon Bell accuses Pittsburgh Steelers of racial bias in comparing treatment of Black and White draftees
articles.summary: Le'Veon Bell claims the Pittsburgh Steelers don't pay their black draft picks while paying white ones, but the facts tell a very different story.
articles.body: Le'Veon Bell is among the Pittsburgh Steelers most productive running backs of all time, joining a list that includes multiple Hall of Famers. But as an observer of how his former teams do business, Bell put himself in the Hall of Shame on Thursday. Bell, who played for the Steelers from 2013-17, saw his former team trade cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys overnight after a contract dispute and decided it was all about race. Because Porter is Black. No, seriously. JERRY JONES GOES ALL IN AS COWBOYS TRADE FOR STEELERS' JOEY PORTER JR IN HOPES OF SUPER BOWL PUSH "I wish Pittsburgh paid their black superstars they drafted just like they pay their white ones they draft," Bell posted on X on Thursday afternoon. " ... hate to see porter get traded .. I thought same thing with [George] pickens? TJ Watt is worth every penny tho, so let's not get it confused .. but something needs to change." Now, Bell has said some wild stuff in the past. But someone needs to jar Bell's memory and adjust his grasp of facts to get him off this race-baiting narrative. Bell, you see, is not an honest broker. He was drafted in the second round by the Steelers in 2013 and after three 1,000-yard-plus seasons, the Steelers tried to pay him. A lot. What matters is that Bell lived through a negotiation where he, as a Black Steelers draft pick, was offered a lucrative contract by the Steelers. And still on Thursday he's saying the Steelers don't pay their Black draft picks like they do their White ones. The racist undertones of Bell's post also flies in the face of the fact that the Steelers, at the time of his offer, were coached by Mike Tomlin, who coached the team for 19 years until he stepped away this year. Someone challenged Bell about these facts beneath his post. And the former running back, who may be suffering from too many blows to the head, shot back that none of those players were drafted by the Steelers. articles.title: DeVonta Smith Injured, Latest News on Eagles WR's Status vs. Rams Amid Hamstring Issue
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles might be without their top wide receiver this week.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles might be without their top wide receiver this week.

Per ESPN's Tim McManus, there isn't "much optimism" that DeVonta Smith will play against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday as he continues to deal with a hamstring injury.

Smith has had a strong start to the season, hauling in 19 catches for 235 yards and a touchdown. He had a 117-yard performance against the Tennessee Titans in Week 2 before recording 65 yards last week against the Chicago Bears.

Smith also missed practice last Thursday before ramping up to play against the Bears, but it appears his chances of doing that again this week are slim.

Being without Smith would severely limit the Eagles' offense, and tight end Dallas Goedert is also likely to miss Sunday's game because of an MCL sprain he suffered in Week 2. Despite missing last week, Goedert is the team's third-leading receiver with 81 yards and a pair of touchdowns.

Hollywood Brown is also questionable this week because of an ankle injury.

With multiple receivers seemingly set to miss the game against the Rams, Philadelphia will need Dontayvion Wicks to take on even more of the workload. The first-year Eagle has nine receptions for 179 yards and a touchdown so far.

Additionally, Philadelphia will need to look to rookie receiver Makai Lemon more often after his slow start to the season, as well as Zach Ertz in the backup tight end role.

The Eagles came into the season hoping to make a case as Super Bowl contenders, but they haven't looked the part so far. Philadelphia had shaky performances against the Commanders and Titans before being blown out by the Bears, who were without starting quarterback Caleb Williams.

The Eagles will face one of the NFL's top teams this week, and potentially being without Smith will make things even more difficult.

articles.title: Eli Manning Gets Blunt on J.J. McCarthy After Vikings-Giants Trade
articles.summary: Former Minnesota Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy likely hopes this trade to the New York Giants sparks a fresh start and helps him prove he’s a starting NFL signal-...
articles.body:
Former Minnesota Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy likely hopes this trade to the New York Giants sparks a fresh start and helps him prove he's a starting NFL signal-caller. In Minnesota, McCarthy had only a handful of starts, along with an injury history and rollercoaster play.Nonetheless, he's still only 23 years old, and perhaps the Giants can unlock the potential that made him a Top 10 pick, which is something the Vikings couldn't do and decided to cut ties by trading him for a 2027 fifth-round pick. With McCarthy in New York, former Giants QB Eli Manning shared his thoughts on the former first-round pick. McCarthy now has to prepare for his opportunity behind starting QB Jameis Winston, who has been shaky since taking over for Jaxson Dart after the starter's season-ending injury. "He's a young kid," Manning said during a Sept. 30 appearance on "The Colin Cowherd Podcast." "For whatever reason, it did not work in Minnesota. But the kid's 20-something, 21, 22 years old, and it's a lot thrown at you. So I think it's just a fresh start coming in this year. I don't think they're, I don't know the game plan, but I don't think he's expected to come in and, hey, you're going to start playing right away. "You got Jameis Winston, a veteran. Give him time. Hey, learn the system, be around, just relax a little bit, and who knows? Just kind of a restart and give this guy a chance. Maybe down the road, he could be a backup for a little bit, be a project and see what happens. He's had success and is a young kid, and I think there's a chance he can make this a turnaround opportunity."

Giants OC Matt Nagy on Former Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy

Meanwhile, Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy shared his early verdict on what he's seen from McCarthy since the trade on Sept. 28."He's done well since he's been here," Nagy told reporters on Oct. 1. "I didn't do a whole lot on him coming out, so I didn't know a whole lot about him, but I talked to a lot of people, got a lot of good reviews back from it, and I think that really the last 48 hours that he's been here, just like most guys, they're going to come in here and grind and then dig into it. "It's crazy because you're basically taking all of OTAs, just trying to learn the foundation, which guys have done in five or six months, and now taking that into two days. So he's done a great job with it. We're impressed. It's impressive. But at the same point in time, too, we also understand that it can be a lot. So there's a little bit of a balance."

Why Giants Decided to Trade for J.J. McCarthy

Furthermore, Amazon Prime's NFL insider, James Palmer, recently shared why New York opted to pursue McCarthy over other options to improve their depth after Dart's season-ending injury. "The other part is playing style," Palmer said in a Sept. 29 video on his X account. "That played a big part because Matt Nagy and that entire offensive staff spent the entire offseason coming into town with John Harbaugh and putting into place an offense that was designed around a quarterback who is mobile, a quarterback who can use his legs, a quarterback who can kind of throw on the move. "Those are things that Jaxson Dart was great at, and those are things that J.J. McCarthy can do as well. That's why you see oftentimes there are a lot of similarities in some buildings between the backup and the quarterback's strengths in this."

articles.title: Bills QB Josh Allen just made NFL history no player has before

articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are sitting pretty at 3-0 to start the season, and quarterback Josh Allen has a good deal to do with that success. The MVP-winning quarterback is already clocking impressive numbers and making a statement as he tries to take this franchise all the way.

Now, Allen is getting respect in the NFL. Not that he didn't have it before, but it's continuing for the 2026-27 season.

In a piece for CBS Sports, Garrett Podell ranks each of the NFL's quarterbacks going into Week 4 . "A quarterback's resume and their performance throughout the season, not just week to week, are parts of the formula used by yours truly to concoct these rankings," he says.

Josh Allen remains among the NFL's top quarterbacks

He has Allen at No. 4 on this tally. While that's good, he's actually down three spots from last week because of turnovers.

"Josh Allen and the Bills' offense were stuck in the mud for much of the day in their 24-16 win over the now 0-3 Los Angeles Chargers ," he notes in the piece. "The team committed five turnovers with Allen responsible for three of them (two interceptions and a lost fumble)."

But, here's where the good stuff starts. Per Podell, Allen is the very first player in NFL history with five-plus passing touchdowns and five-plus rushing touchdowns through the first three games of a season. "That's good enough to remain in the top four," he says.

So, Allen has some things to work on. But, overall, the Bills' fanbase has nothing to complain about yet.

"I'm fully responsible," he told reporters Thursday. "... I spend zero time trying to avoid blame. It's quite the opposite."

McDaniel, who was fired by the Miami Dolphins in January, hoped to use his offensive mind to make the Chargers Super Bowl candidates, but that hasn't been the case thus far.

Los Angeles ranks in the bottom half of the NFL in yards per game (349.3) and ranks fourth-to-last in points per game (14.7).

Herbert has thrown for 627 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions through three games.

Despite the Chargers' struggles, head coach Jim Harbaugh said this week that he has no plans to take some of the offensive control from McDaniel.

"No, we trust Mike. We believe in Mike," Harbaugh told reporters .

This week will be the biggest test so far as the Chargers go up against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks, who have had one of the best defenses in the NFL early on.

articles.title: Kyle Shanahan Explains 'Screw It Play' Call That Led to 80-Yard 49ers TD vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan detailed the team's 80-yard touchdown in which Deebo Samuel took a lateral from Mike Evans into the end zone during a 36-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 3.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan detailed the team's 80-yard touchdown in which Deebo Samuel took a lateral from Mike Evans into the end zone during a 36-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 3.

"For lack of better words, it was just a screw it play," Shanahan explained during a Thursday appearance on KNBR's Dirty Work podcast. "I'm frustrated we're about to go three-and-out. We're in third and 13, which is usually a surrender down where you call a screen or a draw. I was really pissed that we had a false start the first play, I didn't want to go three-and-out at all and that was the best chance to get one. So, you just kind of throw it out there. If you do it every week, it's never gonna work so you try to do it on certain occasions."

"I never went into that game at all thinking, 'Hey, I'm gonna do this on the first third down,'" he added. "But it was just an impulsive thing that ended up working out."

On third down with 12 yards to gain during San Francisco's opening drive of the game, Evans hauled in a pass from Brock Purdy and was about to be tackled short of the sticks.

Before Evans was brought down completely, he pitched the ball back to Samuel for the 80-yard score.

After the win, Samuel revealed that the 49ers didn't practice the play often in the week leading up to the game.

"Oh, it was crazy because we walked through that play like once this week," Samuel said, via David Bonilla of 49ers Web Zone. "It was kind of crazy. We called it [while] kind of backed up. It was third-and-long. Once I seen Mike catch the ball and it was two guys on him, I was like, if I get around here, it ain't gonna be nobody. And [Cardinals safety] Budda [Baker] showed up, and [I] showed the speed that people don't think I got."

Samuel finished the game with 80 yards despite not hauling in a reception, representing the most receiving yards in NFL history in a game in which the player had zero catches (h/t ESPN's Nick Wagoner ).

Shanahan and the 49ers' offense have started the 2026 season on a high note, ranking No. 2 among all teams by averaging 32.7 points per game.

With the win over Arizona, San Francisco improved to 3-0.

The offense had picked up a first down through a penalty and was facing first-and-10 near the Browns’ 20-yard line when Rodgers appeared to grow impatient with the delay in getting the next call.As the play clock continued to run, Rodgers looked toward the Steelers sideline with his arms out and made his frustration clear.“What the F*ck?!”The broadcast then cut toward McCarthy on the sideline. He appeared to mouth, “F*cking A**hole,” although the coach’s response was not clearly audible on the broadcast. That distinction matters. Rodgers’ words were caught by the hot mic, while McCarthy’s response was inferred from what he appeared to say.The timing made the scene even more noticeable. Pittsburgh had spent much of the drive moving the ball, but the play-call delay created an obvious disconnect between quarterback and coach. The disagreement did not derail the possession, either. Four plays later, Rodgers found Roman Wilson for a 12-yard touchdown that put the Steelers ahead 7-0.Why is the Rodgers-McCarthy exchange getting so much attention?The history between Rodgers and McCarthy gives the moment another layer. McCarthy coached Rodgers during the quarterback’s long run with the Green Bay Packers, and the pair won Super Bowl XLV together. Their reunion in Pittsburgh this season marked their first time working together in eight years.There had already been signs that the two were keeping their offensive conversations direct. Following Pittsburgh’s Week 2 loss to New England, Rodgers said he needed to do a better job of making sure McCarthy knew what was working and what was not when it came to play calling. McCarthy had also described their weekly offensive meetings as candid, noting that Rodgers brings experience from several different offensive systems.That makes Thursday’s outburst notable without necessarily proving there is a larger rift. The footage shows frustration in a specific game situation. It does not establish what either man thought beyond that moment.Still, it was impossible to miss. Prime Video’s microphones caught Rodgers’ complaint clearly, cameras picked up McCarthy’s apparent response, and the exchange became one of the most talked-about moments of the Steelers’ night. articles.title: How DK Metcalf turned NFL stardom into a $30 million net worth with a $132 million Steelers contract and lucrative endorsements
articles.summary: DK Metcalf's net worth sits at an estimated $30 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth.
articles.body: DK Metcalf's net worth sits at an estimated $30 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth. That figure looks small next to the four-year, $132 million extension he signed with the Pittsburgh Steelers in March 2025 after a trade from Seattle. The deal includes a $30 million signing bonus and $60 million guaranteed at signing. Add endorsements with Gatorade, Nesquik and eBay, and the gap between contract value and net worth starts to make sense. Much of the Steelers money is still to be paid, and the estimate may lag behind it.How did DK Metcalf build a $30 million net worth?Metcalf's money story started modestly. As the 64th pick in 2019, he signed a rookie deal worth about $4.6 million with a $1.4 million signing bonus. That was modest for a player who would break Seattle's single-season receiving record in 2020 with 1,303 yards.The first real jump came in July 2022. Seattle gave him a three-year, $72 million extension with $58.2 million guaranteed and a $30 million signing bonus. At $24 million a year, that deal is likely where most of his wealth was built, and it matches the $24 million salary Celebrity Net Worth lists.Still, net worth is not salary added up. Taxes, agent fees and living costs take a big share of every NFL paycheck. That helps explain why a player with years of eight-figure pay is pegged at $30 million.What is in DK Metcalf's $132 million Steelers contract?Pittsburgh acquired Metcalf from Seattle for a second-round pick and signed him to a four-year, $132 million extension, the biggest contract in franchise history. It averages $33 million a year. The $30 million signing bonus and $60 million guaranteed at signing matter most for his bank balance, because that money is locked in.The deal has already been tested. Metcalf received a two-game suspension in December 2025 after striking a Detroit Lions fan. It could have voided about $45 million in future guarantees, but Jay Glazer reported the Steelers chose not to. Before the 2026 season, Pittsburgh also restructured the contract, turning part of his base salary into a signing bonus. That freed nearly $18 million in cap space and did not cut his pay.That timing matters for the $30 million figure. The Celebrity Net Worth page shows a March 2025 update date, so it may not fully count the Steelers signing bonus and the Pittsburgh paychecks that followed.Does DK Metcalf earn money from endorsements?Yes, though endorsements likely make up a smaller piece of the picture. Celebrity Net Worth lists Gatorade, Nesquik and eBay among his brand partners. Exact fees are not public, so any figure on that side is a guess. What is clear is why brands like him. The colored mouthpieces, the visor and the occasional blue hair make him easy to spot, and his 4.33-second 40-yard dash at the 2019 combine still gets shared online.His profile also got a lift off the field. He announced his engagement to singer Normani in March 2025, which put his name in entertainment headlines as well as sports ones.Production still drives that value, though. Metcalf did not reach 1,000 yards in his first Pittsburgh season, yet he stayed one of Aaron Rodgers' most reliable targets and helped the Steelers make the playoffs. articles.title: Browns Beat Steelers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Aaron Rodgers, Deshaun Watson, Top Performers
articles.summary: Andre Szmyt boomed a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left to give the Cleveland Browns a 27-24 home victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers in an AFC North battle on Thursday Night Football.
articles.body:
Andre Szmyt boomed a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left to give the Cleveland Browns a 27-24 home victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers in an AFC North battle on Thursday Night Football .

Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Calls on Fringe Stars

Top takeaways from Browns' win over Steelers

The 2-2 Steelers were 2.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook . However, the 3-1 Browns scored 21 straight second quarter points and then engineered a late game-winning drive after Pittsburgh tied the score at 24 to earn their third straight win.

Here's a look at Cleveland and Pittsburgh's notable offensive performers.

Pittsburgh got on the board first when quarterback Aaron Rodgers found wide receiver Roman Wilson for a 12-yard score to cap a 17-play, 78-yard drive.

Cleveland responded early in the second quarter when running back Jaleel McLaughlin scampered for a 28-yard score to help tie the game at seven.

After a three-and-out, Watson immediately found wide receiver Denzel Boston for a 60-yard gain.

Three plays later, running back Quinshon Judkins ran in for a two-yard TD.

Pittsburgh drove down the field in response, but Chris Boswell missed a 48-yard field goal. Cleveland took advantage and went 62 yards in 11 plays, with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. catching a two-yard touchdown pass.

Boswell made his second field goal attempt (from 31 yards out) to slash Cleveland's lead to 21-10 at halftime.

The third quarter was scoreless as five drives ended in four punts and a lost Watson fumble forced (and recovered) by Steelers edge-rusher T.J. Watt.

Pittsburgh got the offense moving early in the fourth quarter when Rodgers found wideout DK Metcalf for 43 yards.

Rodgers soon found tight end Darnell Washington for a 21-yard score with 10:10 left. A two-point try failed, keeping the Cleveland lead at 21-16.

Szmyt's 44-yard field goal put Cleveland up 24-16 with 6:37 remaining.

Both teams traded punts, giving Pittsburgh the ball with 3:32 left. Rodgers led the Steelers down the field and found Metcalf for 50 total yards on two catches.

Pittsburgh's offense stalled deep in Cleveland territory, and the Steelers found themselves with a 4th-and-10 on the Browns' 11-yard line. Rodgers' pass in the end zone to tight end Darnell Washington fell incomplete, but safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren was flagged for defensive pass interference. On the next play, Rodgers hit tight end Pat Freiermuth for a three-yard score.

Rodgers then rushed up the middle for the two-point conversion to tie the game.

However, the Browns then went 36 yards in seven plays thanks in part to wideout Jerry Jeudy, who caught two passes for 27 yards. Szymt soon sent Cleveland fans home happy.

The Steelers got the ball back on their own 35-yard line with 10 seconds left and a timeout, conjuring images of the Baltimore Ravens' game-winning drive last Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys with seven seconds left.

However, a long Rodgers pass to wideout Roman Wilson was caught by Browns safety Grant Delpit for an interception.

Cleveland won despite committing 14 penalties (for 88 yards). Both teams committed a pair of turnovers. Cleveland won the yardage battle, 372-361.

The Browns have now won their last three games against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (23-19), Carolina Panthers (21-18) and Steelers by a combined 10 points. Each contest has featured a game-winning fourth quarter drive led by Watson, who has thrown for 650 passing yards and five scores (one pick) in his last three matchups.

Browns defenders combined for five sacks. Unfortunately, Cleveland star defensive tackle Mason Graham suffered a left knee injury on the opening series and did not return to the game. Mary Kay Cabot of cleveland.com provided more information on the second-year player, who had four sacks in his first three games.

For Pittsburgh, Watt had another great game, adding a sack, a pass breakup and four solo tackles to his forced fumble and recovery.

Both teams play next on Sunday, Oct. 11 at 1 p.m. ET. Cleveland will visit the New York Jets, and Pittsburgh will host the Indianapolis Colts.

articles.title: Ranking the NFL's remaining international games, starting with Sunday's Colts-Commanders matchup
articles.summary: There are seven international games remaining. Some appear more appealing than others right now.
articles.body:
The NFL's first international game of the 2026 season was a 49ers blowout over the Rams. It might not have been a great game, but it was significant — and surprising.

The second international game of 2026 became an instant classic.

The Ravens and Cowboys traded blows back and forth, with Baltimore winning at the buzzer, giving Rio de Janeiro a terrific first NFL contest in the city. All three Brazil games the past three seasons have been tightly contested, one-score games.

But not every international game figures to hit as hard as that one did. Starting with, well, Sunday's game at London's Tottenham Hotspur Stadium between the Colts and Commanders. The NFL has cut ticket prices for Sunday's game after slow sales, and neither team is helping the draw. Both started slowly, and Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is questionable with an elbow injury.

Thankfully, there appear to be other international games with more broad appeal, even as things can change quickly. We're two games into the International Game series, with 49ers-Rams (Melbourne) and Ravens-Cowboys (Rio) already in the books. Seven foreign games remain, six in Europe and one in Mexico.

With the schedule of the remaining international tilts listed above, here's how the games rank in terms of watchability, star power, game quality and interest:

There is a case to be made for looking too far ahead here. After all, who knows whether the Vikings can keep this up? Will the substation have fully wrecked the Niners' roster by Week 11? These are tangible concerns two months out, with the NFL very much a week-to-week league.

But right now all signs point to this being an important game at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City. Both teams sit at 3-0, and they'd have to really go into the tank for this game not to be somewhat entertaining.

Schematically, this is a heavyweight matchup: Kyle Shanahan's offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. Flores beat Shanahan in their only meeting as head coaches, and Flores' Vikings defense twice held Shanahan's offense to 17 points in Minneapolis. So far, the Vikings have allowed only 41 points, rank first in sacks and are in the top 10 in several categories.

Assuming the 49ers can get healthier at receiver, the offense looks to be in great shape. Brock Purdy is emerging as an early MVP candidate, not taking a sack through three games and averaging 9.5 yards per pass play.

These teams might not remain unbeaten by Week 11, but both are making early playoff pushes.

Outside of the second half in Denver, the Jaguars have done a darned good job showing that their 2025 success was no fluke. Head coach Liam Coen and his offense have been humming, and Jacksonville's defense is making big plays and keeping opponents' scores low.

The Eagles opened the season with a pair of narrow wins over middling teams, and a blowout loss at the Bears has some questioning their credentials. They'll also be coming off a tough game against the Rams prior to facing the Jaguars at London's Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Even with sudden questions about the Eagles, this looks like a matchup of two potential division winners, two talented dual-threat QBs in Trevor Lawrence and Jalen Hurts, and two fiery, offensive-minded coaches in Coen and Philly's Nick Sirianni.

The Jaguars have some British fans now, and you know the Eagles faithful are going to make this trip. The only time the two franchises met overseas, in 2018, the game drew a then-record Wembley Stadium crowd of 85,870. There will be some buzz for this game.

The 0-3 Texans don't look great, which makes putting them this high a real risk. Then again, Houston was 0-3 last season and ended up 12-5 and getting a wild-card playoff spot. The Jaguars' 2-1 start certainly puts them in the pole position, but their meeting with the Texans at Wembley Stadium will be their first vs. an AFC South opponent — and this is considered a "home" game for Jacksonville.

If the Texans fall to 0-4 with a home loss to the Cowboys on Sunday, they would drop on this list, too; that hole might be too deep to come back from, with the division almost completely out of reach. But if they beat the Cowboys and take care of business against the Titans, the Texans could be trying to get back to .500 against the Jags.

Right now it looks only half good on paper, but here's betting the Texans figure out a way to be more competitive prior to this overseas divisional matchup. They have little other choice.

Another leap-of-faith pick to a degree. The Patriots have come out of the blocks slowly, especially offensively, with Drake Maye the subject of many armchair evaluators' scrutiny. Even the 2-1 Lions have raised questions about their viability given that they've allowed 24 points or more in every game and were a few snaps away from being 0-3.

That's the pessimistic view. The optimist might say both teams have more manageable games between now and then and can enter Munich week playing better than they are now, especially if the Patriots have A.J. Brown and the Lions have Brian Branch back from injury.

And though this is considered a Lions home game, and Amon-Ra St. Brown is a household name among German NFL fans, the Patriots have played in the country previously and have been designated as one of the NFL's International Home Marketing Area teams for Germany for the past five years.

Either way, it should be a spirited game, even if one or both teams are below where we thought they might be by Week 10.

This is a game that could be far better than expected, or worse for that matter.

A lot depends on how Michael Penix Jr. handles the starting role. He was strong in his Week 3 season debut, giving the Falcons a new outlook on their season after the 0-2 start. With Penix playing well, this Falcons team has some firepower. Atlanta also could be getting James Pearce Jr. back from his suspension, as he's due to be reinstated on Nov. 2. The Falcons also could have cornerback A.J. Terrell (groin) back before this game.

The Bengals were looking terrific prior to the Week 3 loss to the Steelers. They have two tough games (Jaguars, Ravens) and two easier games (Dolphins, Titans) prior to heading to Spain. Cincinnati has been one of the least-injured teams to this point of the season, and it could get a boost with the possible return of WR Andrei Iosivas and CBs Ja'Sir Taylor and Jalen Davis.

At full power, both of these teams are capable of delivering offensive explosions. Again, this could end up far higher on the list by the time this game rolls around.

The Saints were headed for a 2-1 record before blowing a fourth-quarter lead and imploding at home. The Steelers were staring 1-2 in the face before rallying with a statement win over the Bengals.

How good are these teams? Each might be capable of making a playoff push, but the early results have been chaotic. This also could just as easily be a matchup of two teams that fall outside the postseason race. At the least, Aaron Rodgers gives this game name value, and Saints QB Tyler Shough is among the league leaders in passing through three games.

Regardless of where the teams are a month from now, there will be excitement over the first game in France, played at Stade de France, the country's biggest sports venue. This is considered a Saints home game, and they have international marketing rights for France, with obvious connections to the country.

Laissez les bons temps rouler ? We'll have to see which team will have a true home-field edge in Paris, given how well the Yinzers travel. And whether both teams are still competitive by then.

Jayden Daniels is in London, but it's hard to imagine him playing. The Commanders appear ready to turn to Marcus Mariota for this weekend's game. The good news is that Mariota played well enough in Daniels' absence last weekend to lead a rousing, perhaps season-saving win against the defending champion Seahawks.

The Colts also avoided an 0-3 start with their dramatic victory over the Texans in Week 3. Their pass defense will be tested, even against a backup QB, and there's concern over Daniel Jones' turnover rate (five in three games), but this offense can still function with Jonathan Taylor as the lead option.

The buzz for this game has been predictably flat, an expectation from two 1-2 clubs with negative point differentials, kicking off at 9:30 a.m. ET. Daniels' injury dropped the buzz factor down a notch or two as well. It might not have been atop the list had he been healthy, but it's clear there's less of an appetite for this game than any other on the list — at least as things stand now.

articles.title: 2026 NFL Week 4 Biggest Takeaways for Every Team
articles.summary: Week 4 provides teams around the NFL an opportunity to prove whether they're included among the haves or have nots as the 2026 campaign makes it way around the quarter bend.
articles.body:
Week 4 provides teams around the NFL an opportunity to prove whether they're included among the haves or have nots as the 2026 campaign makes it way around the quarter bend.

Entering the weekend slate, five teams remain undefeated and five teams are winless. A lot can be ascertained through the early portion of the season. Though last year's Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans reminded everyone that no certainty exists after reversing their early-season starts.

Still, no one expected the Cleveland Browns to start the season with a 3-1 record, as they did thanks to a victory Thursday over the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Bleacher Report NFL analysts Brent Sobleski , Kris Knox , and Moe Moton will followall of the action then break down each contest, provide takeaways and ask the most pressing questions.

Rookie WRs Highlight Surging Cleveland Browns Offense

The quarterback position has been at the forefront of every conversation regarding the Cleveland Browns for so long that the amount of young talent currently found on the roster has been overshadowed. After Thursday's victory and Deshaun Watson playing well for three straight games, everyone else is going to get far more attention.

General manager Andrew Berry drafted wide receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston 15 selections apart from one another. They've already showed they're high-end targets in their first year. So much so, Jerry Jeudy has become an afterthought.

Concepcion and Boston combined for 153 yards Thursday as Cleveland's top two receivers. Concepcion provides significant juice to create after the catch, while Boston, who led all rookies in receiving yardage entering Week 4, is a legitimate big-bodied target as an X-receiver.

Watson may be playing better than expected, but he's getting a lot of help from two talented, young pass-catchers.

Injury Derails Mason Graham's Ascent to Superstardom

Last year's fifth overall draft pick had been nearly unblockable during the first three weeks of play. Unfortunately, he left Thursday's contest after getting his left leg rolled up and didn't return.

Graham's potential loss for any period of time will revamp Cleveland's defensive front. With Myles Garrett no longer in the lineup, the second-year interior tackle has been a consistently disruptive presence. Maliek Collins and Mike Hall Jr. both made plays throughout the night, but Graham had performed at an elite level to start the campaign.

Any absence will also place a brighter spotlight on Jared Verse, who has yet to record a sack and failed to settle in as the squad's defensive tone-setter.

The wide receivers' inability to create easy throws for 42-year-old quarterback Aaron Rodgers has been common theme through the Pittsburgh Steelers' first four games. Almost everything in their passing game has been difficult to generate, because the team's targets lack explosive traits.

Outside of DK Metcalf, whom opponents are keying to limit his options, the Steelers are searching for anyone to make a play. Pittsburgh's offense had the same problem last season. General manager Omar Khan added veteran Michael Pittman Jr. and drafted Germie Bernard to rectify the situation. Those two produced a combined 26 yards against Cleveland.

As Sumer Sports' Sam Bruchhaus noted after three quarters of play, the Steelers' receivers created separation on only 14.7 percent of their routes. Rodgers is basically asked to make a perfect throw every time he drops back to pass.

RB Jaylen Warren Remains a Bright Spot As bad as the Steelers' passing game is at times, Pittsburgh's running game has been impressive, particularly over the last two games. Jaylen Warren always had spring in his step, with the ability to create after contact and produce chunk plays. The 27-year-old ball-carrier followed last weekend's 127-yard outing with 93 against the Browns' stingy defense. Warren averaged 5.5 yards per carry. The Steelers couldn't really stick to their run game, because they trailed for most of the second half. Even so, Warren should clearly be the team's offensive focal point as the season progresses.

Thursday's action opened with a divisional contest between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns. It'll end the with another rivalry, when the New Orleans Saints host the Atlanta Falcons for Monday Night Football . In-between those two points, only two division matchups will take place. Three games will feature opponents with winning records, highlighted by the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs facing the undefeated Las Vegas Raiders.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy exchange F-bombs early in Steelers loss to Browns
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy had a tense exchange in the middle of a drive. Then the Steelers scored a TD.
articles.body:
Those two lovebirds, Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy, were at it again Thursday night.

The Steelers were driving against the Cleveland Browns in a scoreless game in the first quarter, and Pittsburgh had just gotten a first down by penalty, very much in business at the Cleveland 20-yard line.

But Rodgers apparently didn't get the play call fast enough for his liking. This led to Rodgers and McCarthy exchanging pleasantries — within range of Amazon Prime's boom mics:

Whatever McCarthy called on that play didn't work out well: an incomplete pass. But everyone put that aside, and four plays later, Rodgers hit Roman Wilson on a 12-yard pop pass touchdown to give the Steelers the early 7-0 lead. In the end, despite a strong night from Rodgers, the Browns kicked a field goal in the final seconds to eke out a 27-24 win .

Rogers finished 22 of 40 for 299 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions.

When asked about his portion of the exchange, McCarthy apologized for his choice of words but seemed to suggest it was a heat-of-the-moment thing.

"Communication sometimes is not the best choice of words, but everybody's competing on the field," McCarthy said. "I think, you know, what's said on the field, the way I grew up in this game, you know, usually stays on the field.

"That's not the case today. I understand that. But, yeah, any negative communication on my part, I wish I wouldn't use those words."

Rodgers was not specifically asked about the exchange with McCarthy.

The Rodgers-McCarthy relationship — their first time working together since their Green Bay Packers days eight years ago — has had some testy moments recently. After the Week 2 loss to New England, Rodgers said he needed to do a better job "making sure Mike knows what's working, what's not working" as far as play-calling goes.

McCarthy had been fairly restrained comparatively. Until Thursday, that is.
