articles.title: Browns Troll Mike Tomlin, Steelers with Minecraft Post After TNF Win
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-24 on Thursday and then proceeded to troll former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin's Minecraft city reveal on social media.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-24 on Thursday and then proceeded to troll former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin's Minecraft city reveal on social media.

There is some history between Tomlin and the Browns, of course.

For starters, Tomlin's Steelers went 28-10-1 (including playoffs) when he ran the team from 2007-2025.

The ex-Steelers leader also caught the attention of Browns head coach Todd Monken earlier this offseason after Week 1, when Cleveland lost 34-10 to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Tomlin, now an analyst for NBC's Football Night in America , quoted former Steelers wide receiver Juju Smith-Schuster later that evening by saying, "The Browns is the Browns."

Monken had this to say the following week after the Browns beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 23-19.

Monken did make clear to ESPN's Pat McAfee that he had a "ton of respect" for Tomlin.

Fast-forwarding to Wednesday, Tomlin began sharing his incredibly impressive Minecraft city to the world.

One night later, the Browns got a huge win over Tomlin's former team and couldn't help but reference the Minecraft city afterward.

articles.title: ‘Tom Brady Never Looked as Old as Aaron Rodgers,’ ‘Sad to Watch’ — Ex-Eagles Boss Joins NFL World in Criticizing Steelers QB in Sloppy Loss to Browns
articles.summary: The start of the season has been an absolute rollercoaster for the Pittsburgh Steelers. At 2-2, they have a wildly impressive win over the Cincinnati Bengals...
articles.body:
The start of the season has been an absolute rollercoaster for the Pittsburgh Steelers. At 2-2, they have a wildly impressive win over the Cincinnati Bengals, but also dreadful losses against the New England Patriots and now the Cleveland Browns.

Their latest performance, though, raised a lot of concerns about the state of their quarterback, Aaron Rodgers. In his final season, he had a particularly brutal outing on Thursday Night Football, drawing the ire of fans and analysts on social media.

Aaron Rodgers Is Having a Rough Day on Social Media

The Steelers came into this game with a 1-5 record on Thursdays in the 2020s. The hope was that they could change the script, particularly with the momentum from their Week 3 victory over the Bengals.

Alas, they lost 27-24, with Rodgers having far from an excellent game. Throwing for 299 yards and three touchdowns, he had his moments, including the quarterback sneak on the two-point conversion attempt.

However, he also threw two interceptions, including a game-losing one in the final seconds, while being sacked for a loss of 30 yards. As a result, social media was supremely underwhelmed by his performance in primetime.

"It's actually sad to watch Rodgers play," Joe Banner admitted . "He has even lost the mental part of the game."

The former president of the Philadelphia Eagles had one of the most successful runs for an executive in franchise history. During an eight-year run, he led them to the NFC Championship Games and a trip to the Super Bowl. But even Banner couldn't find many positives in Rodgers' outing.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

"Tom Brady never looked as old as Aaron Rodgers looks tonight," Grant Cohn of Sports Illustrated claimed , pointing to the only other quarterback to have some success after the age of 40.

Brady, though, was in a different stratosphere from Rodgers, who has been struggling since his final year with the Green Bay Packers. Brady, on the other hand, led the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to a victory in Super Bowl 55 at 43 years old.

"Getting pretty tired of seeing Rodgers get up all (expletive) off at the sideline after negative plays when he's been responsible for multiple missed opportunities tonight," Chris Mueller of 93.7 The Fan remarked.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

"Aaron Rodgers went from having his best game in half a decade last week… to looking like it's the end of his career this week," Josh Carney of USA Today claimed . "Really poor night."

Jarrett Bailey of SB Nation was particularly witty as he mocked Rodgers, writing, "If the goal of football was to throw the ball 10 yards in front of your receiver, Aaron Rodgers would be having the greatest game we've ever seen."

Jon Ledyard pointed out the sacks as a major part of the problem for the Steelers and Rodgers, as he claimed, "Rodgers is running a clinic on how to sack yourself as a QB."

It remains to be seen if this was a one-week outlier or if the disappointing season is going to continue for Rodgers.

So far this year, he ranks at number 30 in PFN's Quarterback Impact Metric with a 66.4 grade. Notably, his Week 4 showing delivered a QB Impact Score of 72.1.

But fans will try not to lose hope as he finishes his final season before riding off into the sunset.

articles.title: Patriots and 49ers Named Among Suitors for 16-TD WR Over Past Two Seasons
articles.summary: The addition would be a decent one for the Patriots.
articles.body:
To say the season hasn't gone as planned for the New England Patriots would be putting it lightly, as New England hasn't been able to do enough on either side of the ball for a lot of this season.

At the same time, this is still a 1-2 team with a nice win against the Pittsburgh Steelers and just a three-point loss against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

Sunday's Week 3 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars obviously didn't go as planned, and the Patriots lost 35-6. The Patriots offense struggled once again, and with A.J. Brown and others injured, there's an argument that they could use some help on that side of the football.

Bleacher Report recently suggested one way to change that, noting that Quentin Johnston, the Los Angeles Chargers' former first-round pick who hasn't been great in the NFL, could be a possible fix.

"The fourth-year receiver topped 700 receiving yards in each of the past two seasons but has been an afterthought in Mike McDaniel's offense. He has just six catches for 64 yards through three weeks and has watched Tre' Harris take over the WR2 role opposite Ladd McConkey.

"Johnston should still interest receiver-needy teams, though, as he has a high physical ceiling and another year on his rookie contract—Los Angeles did exercise his fifth-year option. Potential Suitors: New England Patriots, San Francisco 49ers," Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report wrote .

Johnston is a decent player based on some numbers he's put up throughout his career.

However, he's also dropped passes at a ridiculously high rate. If the Patriots and Drake Maye could add a player coming off two straight seasons with at least 700 yards and touchdowns for a reasonable price, it wouldn't be a bad idea, but they shouldn't expect him to be a savior.

articles.title: Will Campbell Sends Nine-Word Message to Patriots' Drake Maye Amid Struggles
articles.summary: Maye and the Patriots need to be better in the near future.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots offense has been one of the worst units in the NFL to start the season, now 1-2 on the year.

As the Patriots get prepared to head into the bulk of this tough schedule, taking on the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, a 3-0 Las Vegas Raiders team, and some other promising teams throughout the remainder of the season, that's going to have to change.

The Patriots have many reasons they haven't been able to do enough on that side of the ball, but quarterback Drake Maye has been the biggest issue. Maye hasn't thrown the football at the level anyone expects, now just 51-of-80 for one touchdown and six interceptions.

He has 585 yards, and he hasn't thrown for more than 208 in any of the first three games of the season. He also hasn't been great with his legs, another issue in itself.

While many in the fan base have been frustrated, and it sounds like some of the coaching staff has been too, certain players are still riding with him.

Will Campbell, who also struggled as a rookie last season, sent a short but sweet message to his young quarterback.

"We're riding with him until the wheels come off," Campbell said, H/T USA Today .

Less than nine months ago, Maye looked like one of the bright young stars at quarterback in the NFL.

While things have been very ugly to start this season, it wouldn't make much sense if he just lost all of who he is and suddenly started doing this.

Perhaps there's more to his shoulder injury than people are leading on, as that would seem to make sense as of now.

articles.title: “Wasn’t working for us”: How Odell Beckham Jr.’s Giants comeback ended after just 19 snaps as John Harbaugh explained why the veteran receiver was released
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr.’s second stint with the New York Giants ended on Tuesday after the veteran receiver played only 19 snaps across three games.
articles.body: Odell Beckham Jr.’s second stint with the New York Giants ended on Tuesday after the veteran receiver played only 19 snaps across three games. Beckham did not record a catch and saw just one target during his return to the team that drafted him in 2014. The Giants then released him, leaving John Harbaugh to explain why the reunion never developed into the offensive role Beckham and the team had hoped for.Beckham had worked his way onto the Giants’ 53-man roster after a difficult summer in which he still had to prove he deserved a place on the team. He responded with a strong finish to the preseason, including seven catches for 76 yards in three games, but his regular-season involvement quickly became limited. Why did Odell Beckham Jr.’s Giants comeback fall apart?Beckham entered the season knowing that his roster place was not guaranteed, and Harbaugh had been clear about what he expected from the 33-year-old receiver. The coach wanted Beckham to show he could still perform at a level that would allow him to contribute during NFL games, and Beckham eventually earned his place after impressing late in camp.His regular-season role, however, never matched that preseason progress.Across the Giants’ first three games, Beckham played 19 offensive snaps and received only one target. His lone target came during New York’s 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, September 27, when quarterback Jameis Winston looked his way on a pass that nearly resulted in an interception. Beckham finished the game without a reception.The lack of opportunities became particularly noticeable because Giants fans still wanted to see Beckham involved. During the Titans game, supporters at MetLife Stadium began chanting “OBJ” while the offense was on the field, but the veteran receiver remained on the sideline for most of the afternoon. He played only six snaps in that game, according to NFL reporting.There was also a practical roster issue behind the decision. New York needed to move Braxton Berrios onto the active roster after using him as a practice-squad elevation during each of the first three games. NFL rules prevented the Giants from elevating Berrios again, and he offered value as a punt and kickoff returner in addition to his work at receiver. The Giants subsequently added Berrios and Charlie Jones while releasing Beckham.That left Beckham with little room to establish himself in the offense, particularly with Malik Nabers, rookie Malachi Fields and Darnell Mooney receiving almost all of the wide receiver targets through the first three games. Beckham also did not contribute on special teams, which made his limited offensive role harder for the Giants to carry on the 53-man roster. What did John Harbaugh say about Odell Beckham Jr.’s release?Harbaugh addressed the decision on Wednesday, Sept. 30, during his media availability in East Rutherford, New Jersey, and accepted responsibility for the fact that the Giants could not create a bigger role for Beckham.Per ESPN, Harbaugh said, “Had a great conversation with Odell and it's tough. But we just weren't getting enough. It just wasn't working for us. And like I told him, I wanted to be able to get more. I wanted him to be able to do more. I wanted to get him on the field more.”Harbaugh said he wanted Beckham to play more and believed the Giants had failed to make that happen.“Whatever reason, we weren't able to do it. Put it on us. We weren't able to get it done. At this point in time, that's kind of where we were and we needed to move on.”The coach also rejected the idea that Beckham’s name or the attention around his return influenced the decision. Harbaugh said the Giants needed more from the roster spot and described the move as a football decision rather than an issue with Beckham personally. He also said he hoped his former player would find another team and get the opportunity to contribute.The release brings an abrupt end to Beckham’s second chapter with the Giants, the team that selected him No. 12 overall in the 2014 NFL Draft. His first stint produced 390 catches, 5,476 yards and 44 touchdowns in New York, along with three straight Pro Bowl selections to begin his career.The 2026 return carried a very different story. Beckham had missed the entire 2025 season before joining the Giants and had to fight for his place on the roster. He eventually made the team and even became emotional after learning he had made the final cut, saying he saw the opportunity as a chance to rewrite the final part of his career.Instead, the comeback ended after three games, one target and zero catches. articles.title: 49ers’ Kyle Juszczyk calls out apparent NFL hypocrisy over beer celly controversy
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk is not holding back after the NFL hit him with a $14,926 fine for his touchdown celebration during a 35-13 victory...
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk is not holding back after the NFL hit him with a $14,926 fine for his touchdown celebration during a 35-13 victory over the Miami Dolphins.

In that Week 2 win, Juszczyk hauled in two receptions for 27 yards, including a key six-yard touchdown catch. To celebrate the score, the veteran Pro Bowler performed his signature move: pretending to chug an invisible beverage in honor of his long-standing nickname, "Juice." However, league officials viewed the gesture differently. The NFL sent Juszczyk an official fine letter claiming his hypothetical drink constituted an "offensive demonstration" that simulated chugging a beer and was "in poor taste."

The penalty immediately sparked outrage around football , with former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce leading the charge on his podcast. Kelce slammed the league for penalizing a harmless imaginary celebration while flooding television broadcasts with alcohol advertisements and corporate sponsorships.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Juszczyk didn't hold back either when addressing his appeal process, pointing out the glaring hypocrisy behind the league's disciplinary action.

"Even if it was beer, I don't think that should be a problem with all of the beer endorsements that we have in the NFL," Juszczyk said regarding his hearing. "Even if it was beer, which it wasn't, I still felt like it wasn't an infraction."

He certainly has a point. The NFL aggressively guards its moral image, yet fills its broadcasts, stadium signage, and revenue streams with lucrative official beer partnerships. Expecting players to ignore that contradiction takes impressive mental gymnastics.

Juszczyk never held an actual alcoholic beverage on the field, nor did he break any safety rules. He simply gave the fans in attendance a fun moment after making a great play. Whether the league rescinds the fine on appeal remains uncertain, but Juszczyk made his voice heard loud and clear . The "No Fun League" struck again, but the fullback got the last word on their selective morality.

articles.title: NFL Week 4 International Series Best Player Props—Colts Vs. Commanders
articles.summary: Find out why Josh Downs and Tyler Warren have appealing receiving yardage player props in Sunday morning's NFL Week 4 International Series contest in London.
articles.body:
NFL Week 4 is the first to feature a Sunday morning game from the NFL's International Series. The Indianapolis Colts are 3.5-point favorites against the Washington Commanders. The quarterback situation is murky for the Commanders, as Jayden Daniels has practiced this week , but Marcus Mariota is waiting in the wings if Daniels is out again.

There's no mystery for the Colts. Daniel Jones is their starting quarterback, and he could be busy this week, which is ideal for the receiving outlook for two of his pass-catching weapons. The team's top healthy wide receiver and their second-year tight end have eye-catching player props in London on Sunday.

NFL Week 4: International Series (London) Best Player Props

Josh Downs Over 60.5 Receiving Yards (-125) at Fanatics Sportsbook

Tyler Warren Over 46.5 Receiving Yards (-114) at FanDuel Sportsbook

Josh Downs wasn't deployed as a full-time wideout during his first three years in his career, with a 64.3% snap share and 67.8% route participation rate. He was also largely limited to the slot, with an 83.1% slot rate and only a 15.9% wide alignment rate through his first 47 NFL games.

Things have changed for the better for Downs this year. The fourth-year pro has a 79.1% snap share, 83.3% route participation rate, 74.4% slot rate and 23.3% wide alignment rate. He's rewarded Shane Steichen for ramping up his playing time.

Downs has a 24.5% target share, 0.27 target per route rate (TPRR), 31.5% first-read rate, 42.8% air yard share, 4.7 receptions per game, 62.0 receiving yards per game and 2.07 yards per route run (Y/RR). After a disappointing 37 receiving yards in Week 1, Downs has climbed to 72 and 77 receiving yards.

He can maintain his momentum this week. Washington's defense has faced the second-highest pass rate over expected ( 11.6% PROE ) this season. The Commanders have allowed the third-most receiving yards per game (192.0) and the ninth-most yards per target (9.39) to wide receivers in 2026.

The Commanders have allowed one wide receiver to surpass 60.5 receiving yards in all three games this year, permitting 73 to Dontayvion Wicks in Week 1, 153 to CeeDee Lamb in Week 2 and 128 to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in Week 3. Downs should be the latest to crack that threshold against Washington's leaky secondary.

Since the Commanders have a pass-funnel defense, there's room for more than one pass-catcher on the Colts to clear their receiving props. Tyler Warren can also thrive. The second-year pro has averaged only 29.7 receiving yards per game, but his 92.5% snap share, 82.4% route participation rate, 22.4% target share and 0.25 TPRR are all excellent marks.

Warren has a get-right matchup this week through two lenses. First, the Commanders have allowed the seventh-most receiving yards per game (67.3) to tight ends this year and the third-most yards per target (10.10). They've allowed a tight end to exceed 46.5 receiving yards in two of three games, allowing 77 to Dallas Goedert in Week 1 and 69 to AJ Barner in Week 3.

Second, Washington's coverage tendencies favor Warren's receiving outlook. The Commanders have played zone coverage 81.0% of the time and two-high coverage 81.9% of the time this season. Warren has 0.24 TPRR and 1.89 Y/RR on 423 career routes against zone and 0.21 TPRR and 1.32 Y/RR on 294 career routes against two-high coverage.

As a result, Warren should join Downs in clearing his receiving prop in the NFL International Series contest in London this week.

articles.title: Stop piling on Drake Maye. A deep dive look at his struggles, what's failing around him and why Patriots should believe he'll bounce back
articles.summary: Maye and the rest of the Patriots organization have to start rebuilding the floor before it starts sinking even further.
articles.body:
After 490 regular-season points and a surprising, and perhaps premature, run to the Super Bowl in Mike Vrabel's first year and Drake Maye's second year, the Patriots' offense seems to have fallen back to earth through three weeks in 2026. Everything has been diagnosed as the reason for its current ailments: a more difficult schedule, a young quarterback flummoxed as "the league adapted to him," an offense seeing no improvement from returning players, or new faces underwhelming or injured.

As with everything in football, everyone has a portion of the blame pie for the Patriots' lackluster start on offense. Just like everyone has their portion of the credit pie when things are going right.

Who is to blame for this putrid start for the Patriots? Well, not to spoil the hundreds, nay thousands, of words below, but just about everyone in New England has a nice slice on their plates as we enter October.

All data is via TruMedia unless otherwise noted.

Busting myths about why Maye is faltering

Let's start with Maye, who is one of the youngest starting quarterbacks in the NFL. He blistered his way through his second season and capped it off with a second-team All-Pro selection and MVP runner-up. His underwhelming playoff performances have been scrutinized and the "soft" regular-season schedule is often brought up as a reason to not anoint him quite yet as the league's next star quarterback. The schedule discussion took on a life of its own despite the passing defenses Maye faced falling more around league average. It's not like he was facing a MAC schedule (plus the lack of firepower around him, but don't worry, we'll get to that).

There have been theories thrown around to explain Maye's turnover-heavy start to 2026. I've heard that he can't "solve" Cover 6, a two-high coverage that has Cover 2 to one side and Cover 4 to the other. I'll snuff out that theory right away: Maye has absolutely no issues against Cover 6. The numbers thrown around are weighted heavily by facing the Seahawks twice, a team that runs Cover 6 more than anybody and, oh yeah, was one of the best defenses on record last season. The Seahawks are also a team Maye and the Patriots have faced twice over his dreaded "since the start of last year's playoffs" drop-off.

Maye had absolutely zero issues against the Chargers and Texans, or really any defense aside from the second matchup versus the Bills, that ran Cover 6 last season. There is no theme of not being able to read out the defense. There is a theme of the Seahawks dominating with their Cover 6 because it completely wipes out the Patriots' preferred formations and concepts. But, even if you include those two Seahawks matchups, Maye has been about league average in terms of success rate against teams in Cover 6; his 46% dropback success rate is just above the league average of 45.4% since the start of last year, including the playoffs. That mark is above Lamar Jackson, Dak Prescott, Caleb Williams, Joe Burrow and Brock Purdy, for instance. And his explosive pass rate (13.8%) is just below league-average and just below Trevor Lawrence.

Maye's decision-making has actually been, for the most part, quite good, even during this mess of a start. He's been efficient, ranking 12th in dropback success rate among 28 quarterbacks with 50 or more pass attempts, and that's despite playing the toughest defensive schedule so far, per FTN's DVOA. His 46% success rate is above Matthew Stafford, Joe Burrow, Daniel Jones, Jordan Love, Jalen Hurts and Bo Nix. And not a soul is saying Stafford or Burrow is off to a poor start this season!

Down-to-down decision-making matters at the position that touches the football every single play (and I don't mean center, though their decision-making matters, too, but I digress).

The turnovers have been rough. Fumbling will likely always be a thing with Maye, as he has just over 9-inch hands, plays an aggressive style as a thrower and runner, and has led all QBs in fumbles lost after being sacked (8) since he entered the NFL.

The interceptions this season have all been a different story. Each turnover is a different microcosm of a young quarterback pressing, being too aggressive at the wrong moments while also operating in a predictable, archaic scheme that lacks creativity and skill players with any semblance of needle-moving talent. That's especially true with early injuries to the players (and also just general misuse and lack of understanding of those players' skill sets) who were meant to inject life and explosive plays into this offense.

Let's perform an autopsy on each of those six interceptions.

The first interception was a pure force by Maye when there was an easy checkdown available. The second interception was a phenomenal read and play by Julian Love, one of the smartest defenders in the NFL who immediately made a read (he's keying the No. 2 eligible pass-catcher to his side; when that player didn't release vertically, he then read Maye's eyes and made a great play).

The third interception was a prime example of the issues plaguing the Patriots' offense, and that Maye has been compounding: Mack Hollins released his route inside, which ends up convoluting the whole concept. Still, Maye should throw that football away.

The fourth one was a ton of issues. Yes, Maye could get to a checkdown, but it would help to not have pressure in his lap — Maye has been pressured on 42% of his dropbacks so far this season — and it would also help for Hunter Henry to actually look on his route.

The fifth interception should have been a throwaway, but it was also a terrible design and use of personnel. Jaguars defenders even said afterward that they knew exactly what was coming. Travis Hunter, who made the interception, said after the game , "We got those plays in practice. The coach did a great job scheming it up for us. He called the perfect call for us. We all talked and we communicated on my side of the ball and I just made it happen."

And that's on top of Rhamondre Stevenson, not a burner, being used to run the horizontally stretching route (into the short side of the field, mind you), Hollins (the guy in there for blocking) not blocking anybody and Efton Chism III stumbling on his route.

That particular play is a perfect snapshot of everything going wrong with the Patriots: lackluster personnel with a predictable play topped off by Maye compounding the issues by trying to do too much.

And, finally, the sixth interception was the right read against that coverage. But Kyle Williams is 5 yards short on his stutter-stop route and allows the cornerback to get inside of him. Not ideal!

The quarterback has to take care of the football. There's an adage with quarterbacks to "not make a bad play worse." And it's cropped up too often for Maye this season despite his actual down-to-down efficiency and good decision-making. You can point at his EPA right now, but there are other quarterbacks who have started a season with poor EPA because of a high turnover rate in a small sample size of games. I can point at other QBs who have started with comparable or even worse numbers over the first three games, and they turned out more than fine. There's Burrow (whose success rate wasn't even close to Maye's this season) and Lawrence in the 2023 season and Dak Prescott in 2018. So, Maye's EPA may be warped right now because of the turnovers, which have to improve, but his down-to-down efficiency and decision-making have still been more than fine. Especially given the absolute hell he has around him.

Even his other knocks, such as his high scramble and sack rates, are more understandable given the circumstances and the fact that he is one of the best scramblers since he's entered the NFL (and those scrambles are way more understandable when you see what he's working with down the field). He's even been highly efficient, with nine of his 10 scrambles this year resulting in a successful play. Even the sacks he has taken have a silver lining: he doesn't lose a ton of yards, ranking second in yards lost per sack at 4.2.

The underlying issue, though, is that Maye HAS to make high-end throws to generate explosives and HAS to be perfect with the football in an offense that is constantly feeling tight and static as it lacks any creativity in the run and pass games. And it lacks the personnel to help alleviate that pressure.

Here are Maye's throws that have gained 15 or more yards for the Patriots this season. Only two were thrown under 15 yards. His 21.4 air yards per attempt on gains of 15 or more yards is the highest in the NFL.

For comparison, Burrow's air yards is at 15.9 yards on passes that have gained 15 or more yards.

And Patrick Mahomes is at 12 air yards per attempt on his 15-plus yard gains.

It's really nice when you don't have to make constant downfield forays to generate big plays . And Maye has to do it a ton. He did last year, too!

But these throws can lead to volatility, especially if that decision-making gets rushed or the quarterback feels pressed.

Supporting cast and scheme are part of the problem

Looking at the scheme and players around Maye, "underwhelming" is the nice word I'll use to describe it. Henry, never a burner but a steady target for Maye, has taken a noticeable decline in play and athleticism. Henry's speed has dipped over the past few seasons, from a top mark of 18.84 mph in 2024, to 18.12 mph in 2025, to 17.73 in 2026. His average route speed has dropped from 12.06 mph in 2025 to 11.53 this year. And he just hasn't been as reliable.

There is a general lack of juice with the Patriots pass-catchers. Per Next Gen Stats, Henry actually leads the Patriots' pass-catchers in missed tackles forced this year, with 1 (one). There's no tie there, either. That's right, the Patriots' wide receivers have forced the same amount of missed tackles this year as you, dear reader. They have made zero tacklers miss this season. Z-E-R-O. Thirty-year-old Chris Godwin, coming off an injury-riddled season in 2025, has forced five missed tackles this year. Emmett Johnson, the rookie backup running back for the Chiefs, has forced six!

There's hope that reinforcements will be coming soon. A.J. Brown played just over a half before going on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain. Tight end Eli Raridon, who has flashed early as a blocker and receiver in his young career, has also battled a thigh injury and a devastating personal loss (sidebar: please keep the Raridon family in your thoughts). Both players could come back over the next month. So that, and in theory, an easier schedule in terms of defenses over the next few weeks, should help. But there's just the sheer usage of their other skill players that makes me sound the alarm about what's going on with New England's offense.

There's Romeo Doubs, the other offseason addition the Patriots made to the receiver room. And, through three weeks, I have to ask if offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels and the Patriots' coaches watched Doubs and how he was best used in Green Bay. Like, at all.

Doubs, even going back to his time at Nevada, has been best used on breaking routes at the short and intermediate level. His connection with Jordan Love on outbreakers was particularly notable.

What do the Patriots do with Doubs? If you say use him on breaking routes, the obvious answer, you'd be wrong! They instead use him on vertical routes like gos and stops, like he's Randy Moss.

Doubs ran outbreakers on 22.5% of his routes in 2025, per Next Gen Stats. That number is 11.7% this year. And 44.2% of his routes are vertical this season, compared to 31% last year.

This matters! Doubs has been very productive on breaking routes and is around league average on go and hitch/stop routes over the past two seasons, just like he was in college!

Combining his 2024 and 2025 numbers in Green Bay, Doubs had 75 catches on 108 targets for 956 yards on 466 breaking routes (both in-breaking and outbreaking) for a 110.7 QB rating. Doubs averaged 2.1 yards per route on breaking routes, the same number as Justin Jefferson over that time and just below names like Jaylen Waddle, CeeDee Lamb and DeVonta Smith.

He averaged a first down on 12.4% of his routes. That ranks 13th among all receivers with at least 400 routes over that period. He's sandwiched between Ja'Marr Chase and Waddle in the rankings, and well above the league average of 8.8%.

On 249 routes defined as go and hitch routes, Doubs averaged 1.4 yards per route, below the average of 1.5. He recorded a first down on 6.8%, hanging out with receivers like Adonai Mitchell and again hovering around the league average of 6.5%.

Doubs has been targeted just three times on outbreakers this season. The results? Three catches for 100 yards.

It's not just Doubs, either. Williams, who I mentioned before with his lack of details on Maye's last interception, has been pigeonholed as an isolated wide receiver who runs nothing but vertical routes. While Williams was a big-play machine in college, often on vertical routes, those big plays didn't come just as an isolated receiver. But for whatever reason, the Patriots cater their offense to DeMario Douglas and even Hollins. This lack of role diversity impacts their other players, including Williams. He has 22 total routes in his career from the slot, with three targets. Why is that notable? In college, Williams ran 143 routes his last two years at Washington State from the slot while racking up 3.51 yards per route run and 13.3% first downs per route run (compared to 2.34 yards and a 9.3% first-down rate from outside alignment). The NFL is a totally different animal than college, of course. But, for a team lacking big plays, it seems like something to at least try to help create space and get a young player going.

There's even proof of concept for this last year! Williams' 72-yard touchdown against the Buccaneers in Week 10 of the 2025 season came on an over route when he was aligned in a condensed split (a way to "create" a slot when only two receivers are on the field).

If Williams seemingly lacks details with his route-running, it seems like an easy solution to just let him run and use his speed.

It's not just the passing game, either. The Patriots' offensive line and designs in the run game also leave a lot to be desired. The Seahawks exposed the Patriots' pass protection scheme in both recent matchups. Defensive games and twists constantly give them issues, especially with center Jared Wilson and on the right side that has faced injuries.

To their credit, the Patriots have tried to sprinkle in a protection scheme called Dash Pass to move the pocket for Maye, help the protection and let Maye continue to attack downfield.

The run game is still simplistic in its design. It's sound, but sound can go only so far if the players aren't putting it over the top. This is where design and creativity take more importance in a league predicated on matchups.

The Patriots love running the duo run concept, which in itself is not an issue. Duo is good to run in the current NFL ecosystem with how defenses are playing their boxes and coverages. The Patriots have been above average on duo runs in terms of success rate (45.7% compared to the league average of 40.8%). The issue is that they telegraph their duo runs and there are no big plays happening on them. They average only 3.5 yards per carry on duo runs and have been stuffed seven times, the most in the NFL, per Next Gen Stats. They're the only team in the league to average negative yards before contact on duo runs this season. They've played good defenses to start this season, but that's putting a lot on the Patriots' running backs to make something happen.

The Patriots use motion on 45.6% of their early-down runs so far this season, per Next Gen Stats. They use motion at the snap on 26.3% of those plays. Both are dead last in the NFL. Now, motion isn't pixie dust that makes everything better, but it sure can help when the personnel is lacking and defenses are keying on your favorite run plays!

And, just like the Dash Pass in the passing game, there have been flashes of new ideas in the run game. And they've been working! TreVeyon Henderson's long touchdown against the Steelers came on a tackle pull concept (generally known as a dart run concept) that seemed to catch the Steelers completely by surprise because it was such a tendency breaker for the Patriots.

Do that more! Do something different! It won't hurt to try! There has to be better ways to alleviate things for Patriots players who aren't winning on their own.

If you want a play indicative of how offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels is going to play just his hits, no matter the personnel, look at the Patriots running a concept known as "Hoss Juke" for Douglas against the Jaguars. Hoss Juke features mirrored seam routes on the inside and stop routes on the outside, with a "Juke" route over the middle that's meant to isolate the top pass-catcher against a hopeless linebacker. In theory, anyway.

If you need an example of how telegraphed the Patriots' empty formation was, the Jaguars dropped nine defenders into coverage (likely supposed to be eight, but I think dropping nine was fitting).

Maye found Douglas on this play, but Douglas dropped it. In a perfect world, Maye rallies and throws the stop/hitch route to his teammate at the top of his screen. But, pre-snap, I wouldn't like a running back against Travis Hunter, either.

What are the silver linings for the Patriots? The schedule for the offense gets a bit easier starting Sunday. Brown should come back over the next couple of weeks, and same with Raridon. And their defense has actually been doing some interesting things (it currently ranks first in EPA vs. the pass and fifth in success rate, with the run defense being solid, but lacking explosive plays, too).

And the offense has moved the ball fairly well in each game before Maye's turnovers, penalties (like the one that negated a Maye scramble touchdown against the Jaguars) and a missed field goal for good measure. I've laid out issues, but it's definitely not the worst offense ever or even close to it. I use a home-brewed metric called SUPLEX that combines success rate and explosive play rate into a simple measure, and the Patriots rank just below league average, at 21st overall.

And the quarterback will be fine. In fact, I think he will be more than fine, even with the turnovers and weird stuff surrounding his shoulder . (T hat flea flicker in Week 1 wasn't an underthrow , by the way. A.J. Brown just ran his route WAY too early on it and the play was called a bit too close to the end zone for my liking. A common byproduct of running flea flickers is receivers too eagerly running their route before the quarterback even gets the ball).

His down-to-down decision-making has still been fine. And when you look at the start of his career — a sample size that includes the Jerod Mayo experience, a year when Maye finished with the eighth-best rookie season in terms of success rate since 2013 — the start of this year and his "easy" schedule of 2025, Maye has been off to one of the best starts for a young quarterback on record.

No caveats. You can even include his playoff numbers and it still holds up. He ranks third in dropback success rate among the 30 quarterbacks with 1,000 or more pass attempts through their first three seasons since 2013, behind only Mahomes and Brock Purdy. That 49.2% number jumps up to 50.5% if you remove the playoff games.

If you look at just his success rate on throws, he's fourth, including the playoffs, and second when you remove the playoffs. He's also the second-best scrambler in terms of efficiency over that time period while scrambling over 10% of his dropbacks (a number that will need to come down slightly for longevity purposes). He's third in EPA per dropback (see, sample size!). He's seventh in explosive pass rate. He's even second in completion rate, at 68%, for the "accuracy" wonks!

Even looking at all 69 quarterbacks with 1,000 or more pass attempts since 2013, there's Drake Maye well into the top-right. He's next to or above names like Peyton Manning, Josh Allen, Dak Prescott, Philip Rivers, Lamar Jackson, and Purdy (and Jimmy Garoppolo).

The ceiling is there on top of the efficiency. Now Maye and the rest of the Patriots organization have to start rebuilding the floor before it starts sinking even further.

articles.title: Titans' Anthony Hill Jr. named NFL Defensive Rookie of the Month
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. earns NFL Defensive Rookie of the Month honors after a stellar start.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans may have stumbled out of the gate in the 2026 season, but those struggles may have helped them find a star.

Rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. burst onto the scene with an incredible 16-tackle NFL debut against the New York Jets in Week 1, subbing for Cedric Gray, who was in concussion protocol, and hasn't looked back. Over three weeks, the second-round pick out of Texas has led the Titans with 34 tackles and added two quarterback pressures and two passes defensed.

Those numbers earned Hill his first award of the season on Thursday, when he was named the NFL Defensive Rookie of the Month for September.

Hill now joins a short list of former Titans who have earned this honor, and he is only the second defensive player to do so.

Here is the short list of Titans who have earned NFL Rookie of the Month honors.

1996 RB Eddie George (Sept)1999 DE Jevon Kearse (Sept., Nov., Dec.)2008 RB Chris Johnson (Sept)2015 QB Marcus Mariota (Sept)2019 WR A.J. Brown (Dec)

articles.title: Pittsburgh Steelers 24-27 Cleveland Browns: Deshaun Watson leads game-winning drive to set up field goal in final seconds
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson led another game-winning drive while Andre Szmyt landed a career-long field goal in the last 10 seconds for the Cleveland Browns to beat the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-24;  Aaron Rodgers Rodgers completed 22 of 40 passes for 299 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions
articles.body:
Watson, who completed 24 of 33 passes with a touchdown and an interception, was four of five for 46 yards as he led a go-ahead drive in the fourth quarter for the third straight week.

The Browns - who are 3-1 for the first time since 2021 - had a 21-7 lead late in the first half before the Steelers rallied to tie it at 24-all. Aaron Rodgers threw a three-yard touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth with 1-44 remaining and Rodgers sneaked it in for the two-point conversion.

Rodgers, who was 22 of 40 for 299 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions, had one final chance to get the Steelers in field goal range, but he was picked off by Grant Delpit at the Browns' 18 with one second left.

Pittsburgh's Jaylen Warren rushed for 93 yards on 17 carries and DK Metcalf had five catches for 115 yards.

Cleveland's defence sacked Rodgers five times.

Cleveland has won eight straight Thursday night games, the longest active streak and fourth longest in NFL history. Four have come against the Steelers.

Pittsburgh (2-2) is 0-10 on the road against AFC North rivals on Thursdays.

After Cleveland went three-and-out on the opening possession, Pittsburgh went 78 yards in 17 plays, capped by Wilson taking a shovel pass 12 yards around left end on a jet sweep. It was the second straight game in which Steelers have reached the end zone on their first drive.

Watson had 181 yards passing by halftime, his most in the first 30 minutes since joining the Browns in 2022.

Jaleel McLaughlin tied it at 7-7 with 12-14 remaining in the first half on a 28-yard run around right end. The fourth-year running back broke a pair of tackles at the 22 and went through a narrow opening at the 15 before scoring.

The drive was set up after Denzel Ward picked off Rodgers' pass intended for Michael Pittman Jr. at the Browns' 44 on the second play of the second quarter.

Cleveland took a 14-7 lead midway through the second quarter on Quinshon Judkins' two-yard run off right guard. The touchdown came three plays after Watson found Denzel Boston for a 60-yard completion to the Steelers 14 on the first play of the drive.

Harold Fannin Jr. then hauled in his third touchdown in two games on a two-yard pass from Watson on third-and-goal with 1-22 remaining.

It was the first time since Week 13 of the 2020 season against Tennessee that the Browns scored at least 21 points in the second quarter.

The Steelers got within 21-10 on Boswell's 31-yard field goal with eight seconds left before halftime.

Rodgers rolled right and connected with Washington for a 21-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter to bring Pittsburgh within 21-16. The two-point conversion attempt failed. The Steelers fought their way back to level the game but the Browns emerged victorious with a dramatic finish.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Browns' NFL Week 4 Game vs. Steelers
articles.summary: The young Cleveland Browns might not have much experience in the spotlight, but they seemed right at home in a 27-24 Week 4 win on Thursday Night Football.
articles.body:
The young Cleveland Browns might not have much experience in the spotlight, but they seemed right at home in a 27-24 Week 4 win on Thursday Night Football .

Todd Monken's squad moved to 3-1 and the lead in the AFC North with a win that was built around a 21-point explosion in the second quarter, an effective pass rush and just enough playmaking in the final quarter to finish the job.

Let's take a closer look at who shined and who struggled as Cleveland extended its winning streak to three.

Deshaun Watson had one quarter of A+ football and enough negatives from the other three quarters to bring the whole thing down a letter grade.

His first-half statline was his best as a Cleveland Brown and looked reminiscent of his best days in Houston. He was 14-of-17 for 181 yards and a touchdown. He was using his feet to extend plays and finding receivers downfield.

Then the turnovers and lack of ball security crept in. He threw an interception on a throw that was altered by Jack Sawyer in the backfield, lost a fumble and registered another one that was recovered by his own team.

Then he showed a recovery of his own, pulling himself together and making enough plays on the final drive to set up the game-winning field goal. It was a nuanced performance that was enough to get the win.

It remains really difficult to assign credit and blame for the Browns rushing attack (or lack thereof) at this point. Judkins was once again held in check to the tune of 3.1 yards per carry. However, 50 of his 53 yards came after contact, per PFF .

It does appear that Judkins is hit in the backfield often, but he also doesn't seem to be hitting plays where they are blocked either. That being said, his 43 receiving yards can't be ignored.

Sanders was just kind of adequate within his small role on the offense. He had two carries for nine yards and two receptions for seven.

One snap. One carry. One touchdown. McLaughlin's 28-yard scoring run was the run game's best play of the day and it again raises questions about Judkins' struggles to get free.

There was a lot to like about KC Concepcion's game this week. The obvious is that his eight targets were much more productive. He turned eight looks into five receptions for 64 yards.

However, he also made an excellent effort to block Patrick Queen on Jaleel McLaughlin's touchdown run—an encouraging sign from a young, smaller receiver.

Boston followed up a relatively quiet day on Sunday with an impressive performance on Thursday. Boston once again had the longest reception of the game at 60 yards.

He might have had a touchdown if Steelers cornerback Asante Samuel Jr. hadn't gotten away with a bit of holding on a deep ball from Watson.

Welcome to the 2026 football season, Jerry Jeudy. The stat line wasn't gaudy. He had just three catches for 36 yards, but two of them were on the final drive in crunch time.

Top takeaways from Browns' win over Steelers

Fannin got into the end zone for the second consecutive week. His production would have been boosted if Watson hadn't badly overthrown him when he was wide open on 3rd and 8 in the fourth quarter.

Whiteheart was on the field for 22 snaps and wasn't targeted in the passing game. He was fine as a blocker, but also didn't make much of an impact either way.

Fano put together a relatively clean sheet in pass protection with no sacks given up. There were a few edge pressures to come from his side, but he mostly protected Watson well.

Johnson didn't have any glaringly bad reps in pass pro. That put him on a path toward his first good grade of the season.

Unfortunately, he also had a false start on the last drive that cost the team five yards and 10 seconds off the clock.

Wypler was playing for an injured Elgton Jenkins at the pivot. He did a fine job considering some of the play Browns fans have seen from him before. He surrendered a few pressures, but wasn't completely dominated by Keeanu Benton.

Barber overcame a tough matchup and some growing pains last week to post a decent performance against the Steelers. He was solid in pass protection and played penalty-free.

Howard's grade has been abysmal most weeks, but he actually gets some credit here for going against T.J. Watt and holding up to some extent. Watt beat him across the face after getting chipped by the tight end once, but the day wasn't a total disaster overall from Howard.

Verse had the best game of his early Browns career in Week 3, but this one had too many lowlights to ignore. Verse did not get in on the sack party, but did get tricked on the Roman Wilson misdirection jet sweep for a touchdown and jumped offsides when the defense had the Steelers pinned on the one-yard line.

McGuire picked up his second sack in as many weeks. His spin to get back to the inside after Max Iheanachor had washed him out of the pocket is a move that he should continue to go to.

Verse might not have had the best night, but Sam Williams picked up the slack. He made an impact play by hitting Aaron Rodgers' elbow on the Denzel Ward interception in the second quarter and picked up his first sack of the season.

Mason Graham's torrid start to the season was unfortunately derailed on Thursday night. He suffered a knee injury on the Steelers' opening drive and did not return to the game.

Hall continues to be an underrated element of the Browns defensive front. He got in the box score with a sack and was able to generate some pressure as the looper in some stunts.

He left the game at one point with an apparent leg injury, but returned and still made an impact.

Huntington was forced into a larger role by Graham and Hall both getting injured. He responded with a sack and would have had two if one hadn't been negated by a Sam Williams penalty for hands to the face.

Still, Huntington was driven on the quarterback sneak that Rodgers scored on, but he conceded too many run lanes to get a higher grade here.

Collins had a sack where he was schemed to get a one-on-one with the running back. He delivered by bulldozing him and getting the highlight finish to the play.

However, he was also part of the reason that Jaylen Warren averaged 5.5 yards per carry.

Schwesinger was all over the field and put together another strong performance. He didn't have enough highlight-reel splash plays to warrant an A, but he was strong in coverage and racked up nine total tackles.

Williams made a high-leverage play getting to the flats and stopping Jaylen Warren in his tracks on a two-point conversion attempt in the fourth quarter. He was good in pass coverage, but can't get an A based on finding himself out of position on too many of Jaylen Warren's runs.

This is Ward's second A mark in as many games. His interception in the second quarter was teach tape coverage that flipped the momentum at the time. DK Metcalf had a nice night, but that didn't come at Ward's expense.

Tyson Campbell's return from injury was far from triumphant. The Steelers' drive to tie the game was largely predicated on isolating Metcalf on Campbell. The matchup did not go the Browns' way.

The only bright spot was that he tackled better than usual and registered one pass breakup.

Roman Wilson, Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth all had good nights for the Steelers. They all made Harden look bad at different points. Ultimately, the Steelers had a passer rating of 141.4 on the seven times they targeted the slot corner, per PFF .

Delpit gets bonus points for closing out the game with an interception. That was really the cherry on top for the safety, though. He put together a nice game that included six total tackles and a pass defended.

Hickman was not at fault for the success of the tight ends and the slot receiver for Pittsburgh. He didn't make any outstanding plays in coverage, but he was an asset as a run defender.

The rookie saw an uptick in snaps, and there was some good and bad. He had the critical pass interference on fourth down in the red zone while trying to cover Darnell Washington and was beaten for the touchdown by Pat Freiermuth.

But he also defended two passes while collecting four tackles.

MVP! Szmyt continues to be the most reliable Brown every week. He went 2-for-2 on field goals and 3-for-3 on PATs. Most importantly, he drilled the 56-yarder to go ahead with 10 seconds left.

Bojorquez gave the team plenty of margin for error by flipping the field a few times. One of his four punts was downed on the one-yard line.

articles.title: Ranking the Eight Biggest Bills Rivals of All Time
articles.summary: It's Patriots week for the 3-0 Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
It's Patriots week for the 3-0 Buffalo Bills.

If the Bills can slay their biggest contemporary AFC East rival on Sunday, they'll open up an effective 3.5-game lead on New England just four weeks into the 2026 NFL season.

But defeating those pesky Pats is rarely easy for the Bills, who lost to this very team in Orchard Park almost exactly one year ago and haven't beaten New England by more than a score since 2022.

On the brink of the rivalry's latest chapter, here is a definitive ranking of the top eight adversaries in franchise history.

This probably becomes less of a rivalry with each passing season, but there's still some lingering old-school AFC East blood for fans long enough in the tooth to remember when Indianapolis was arguably Buffalo's second-biggest division rival.

That period spanned over three decades before realignment separated the teams in 2002, but they've since played some blockbusters, including a thrilling 27-24 wild-card win by Buffalo in the 2020 playoffs and the 2017 " Snow Bowl ", which ended in a Bills overtime victory in Orchard Park.

This, on the other hand, is almost entirely modern. Both teams found their current franchise quarterbacks in the first round of the 2018 draft. Both have been perennial AFC contenders ever since.

Throughout the era marked by the Chiefs dynasty, Buffalo and Baltimore have been fighting for status as the top challenger to that juggernaut.

Their last two matchups came down to the wire, with Buffalo coming back to win 41-40 in last year's season opener. Then, they held on to beat Baltimore 27-25 in the 2024 playoffs (their second postseason clash this decade).

Lamar Jackson and Josh Allen have won three of the last seven MVP awards combined. Both are prime candidates again this season as Baltimore and Buffalo appear to be on another postseason collision course in a rivalry that only continues to gain steam.

Like the Indy rivalry, this fades as those 1992 and 1993 Super Bowl losses become memories, if not secondhand accounts told to those who weren't alive to see the dynastic Cowboys crush Buffalo's championship hopes in the final years of the Jim Kelly era.

The franchises have met just seven times in the 32 seasons since those Super Bowl tilts, but many Bills fans harbor a special hatred for a glamour franchise that felt like the exact antithesis of blue-collar Buffalo during both teams' 1990s peaks.

One Sentence to Describe Every NFL Team's September 1️⃣

Longevity earns the Jets this spot: the two franchises have been division adversaries since entering the AFL as charter members in 1960.

This is the opposite of the Dallas rivalry (or the Chiefs rivalry we'll look at soon) because it is based on quantity, not quality. The two have met 131 times over the course of 66 years, including once in the playoffs, when Buffalo nearly blew a 24-0 lead to Gang Green in the 1981 wild-card round.

The two have rarely been competitive at the same time, but that heavy history—amplified by their shared "New York" geographic feud—naturally produces plenty of hatred and resentment.

These two Super Bowl-less AFC rivals were originally division rivals in the AFL. So there was shared misery and history long before they broke each other's hearts in two of the most memorable playoff games in NFL history.

The first was " The Comeback ," when the Bills overcame the largest playoff deficit in NFL history to beat the then-Houston Oilers 41-38 in a 1992 wild-card game at Rich Stadium.

Seven years later, Tennessee pulled off the Music City Miracle to stun the Bills in a wild-card victory that kicked off a Super Bowl run.

This rivalry has since faded a bit, but four of their six meetings between 2006 and 2018 were decided by exactly one point.

This feud was so lopsided during the Bill Belichick era that it could hardly be considered a rivalry. As Tom Brady noted on the Chargers-Bills broadcast this past Sunday, he went 32-3 against the Bills during his two decades in New England.

That said, the two go way back to 1960 as division foes. The rivalry might actually be peaking now as both are contenders.

The script was officially flipped when the Bills absolutely demolished the Patriots 47-17 in the 2021 playoffs. It's since become quite competitive overall. The Bills have won six of the last 10 matchups, as each of the last six has been decided by a single-score margin.

We're likely in for another heater on Sunday as the teams meet for the 134th time since both were born in 1960.

The Chiefs have undoubtedly become Buffalo's primary modern rival, as Buffalo-Kansas City has turned into the ultimate battle of the 2020s in this league.

Since 2020, the Bills have 76 regular-season wins and the Chiefs have 75. Nobody else in the NFL has more than 65. Yet Patrick Mahomes has three rings, while Josh Allen has yet to reach a Super Bowl.

A lot of that has to do with the fact that Mahomes and the Chiefs keep stymying the Bills in the playoffs. While Buffalo has defeated the Chiefs in each of their last five regular-season matchups, Kansas City is 4-0 against the Bills in the playoffs since 2020.

The last three of those victories came by an average of four points, with one coming in overtime.

Long before that, they also met with trips to the Super Bowl on the line in 1966 (Kansas City won the AFL Championship Game) and 1993 (Buffalo won the AFC Championship Game). So this isn't entirely new blood.

Miami swept Buffalo 20 consecutive times during the 1970s, setting up pure catharsis in 1980, when Bills fans tore down the Rich Stadium goalposts after Buffalo finally snapped the skid.

But the golden era of this rivalry came when Jim Kelly and Marv Levy consistently battled Dan Marino and Don Shula in the 1980s and 1990s. That's when you really felt the contrast between the Miami beaches and Buffalo snowstorms; the intensity level was often unmatched.

They are polar opposites in geography, culture and climate. While other adversaries have had their eras of dominance, no matchup in franchise history carries deeper, more persistent venom than the one with Miami.

articles.title: One Sentence to Describe Every NFL Team's September
articles.summary: How is it October already?
articles.body:
Granted, one of the latest kickoff dates in modern NFL history made September feel like an absolute blur. But four weeks in, the campaign is no longer young.

On the eve of October's first Sunday, here is a one-sentence reflection on every NFL team's opening month.

Buffalo Bills: They banked three wins in September, but disjointed performances on both sides of the ball leave them feeling far less convincing than their record suggests.

Miami Dolphins: A rough start was entirely expected, but a gritty home battle against Kansas City showed there's a competitive pulse worth building on.

New England Patriots: Strip away last season's element of surprise, unmatched injury luck and comically easy schedule, and New England looks every bit like a team utterly unprepared for life against real-world competition.

New York Jets: They may not be a finished product, but being genuinely competitive every week is an undeniable step forward.

Baltimore Ravens: September confirmed the Ravens' reality remains unchanged—their margin for error begins and ends with Lamar Jackson's magic.

Cincinnati Bengals: The early positives easily outweighed the negatives, but letting another winnable divisional brawl slip away shows this team still lacks a killer instinct.

Cleveland Browns: They've been competitive more often than not, which could hurt the rebuild on paper but is a good omen regarding the new regime.

Pittsburgh Steelers: Any hope that a fresh season and a new head coach would iron out Pittsburgh's chronic inconsistency and unbalanced roster vanished before September even wrapped.

Houston Texans: An overworked defense can only mask so much for an 0-3 team sprinting toward franchise-altering decisions come January.

Indianapolis Colts: They've shown plenty of fight since a flat home opener, but glaring talent deficits at quarterback and on defense will once again cap their ceiling come winter.

Jacksonville Jaguars: Two lopsided September wins and a gritty road showing in Denver proved last season's late-year surge was no fluke.

Tennessee Titans: Real progress meant taking care of business against at least one New York squad, but laying eggs against both proves this rebuild is stuck in neutral.

Denver Broncos: Emerging from a gauntlet against the Chiefs, Jaguars, and Rams at 2-1 is acceptable, but continually spotting opponents early leads is an unsustainable way to live.

Kansas City Chiefs: Roster attrition may test their ceiling come January, but an undefeated start showed an evolved offense capable of hunting another ring.

Las Vegas Raiders: A perfect start against soft competition doesn't instantly make them a true contender, but it probably means Klint Kubiak was the right hire.

Los Angeles Chargers: This isn't working.

Dallas Cowboys: A devastating finish in Brazil cast a dark shadow over an otherwise fine September, putting immediate pressure on this core to prove it wasn't a season-defining defeat.

New York Giants: Few 2-1 starts have ever felt this bleak, as crushing losses to Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns stripped away whatever optimism September was supposed to bring.

Philadelphia Eagles: For a supposed contender, getting outscored by two touchdowns across three games against middling competition is hardly a ringing endorsement of their current formula.

Washington Commanders: Defensive flashes and undeniable grit kept September competitive, but everything in Washington is about to take a back seat to an impending quarterback mess.

Chicago Bears: September in Chicago was pure feast or famine, perfectly captured by a team that somehow never scored or allowed a total between 10 and 25 points.

Detroit Lions: A negative scoring margin in a month with just one road game and two home games against teams with losing records in 2025 is extremely discouraging.

Green Bay Packers: They've played three teams that didn't make the playoffs in 2025 but have yet to win a game in regulation, proving that Green Bay remains at least a tier below true heavyweight status

Minnesota Vikings: Three wins mask a glaring deficiency in an offense averaging a league-low 4.3 yards per play. This is an offensive reality that is not sustainable beyond a soft October slate.

Atlanta Falcons: Whether getting embarrassed by Carolina or demolishing Green Bay was the real outlier remains an open question, but Michael Penix Jr.'s sharp debut left Atlanta feeling encouraged heading into October.

Carolina Panthers: There were more lows than highs in the first month of the season for a team that is still stuck in neutral, nowhere near entering the contender conversation.

New Orleans Saints: September confirmed the Saints are fatally flawed and at least a tier below true contention, but also that they'll be one of the most entertaining teams to watch in the 2026 campaign.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers: An 0-3 start and 10 defeats across their last 12 games confirm the competitive window has slammed shut, leaving an aging roster drifting into irrelevance.

Arizona Cardinals: Growing pains were guaranteed as the rebuild continues, but a mildly encouraging September proved Mike LaFleur's offense isn't what's holding Arizona back.

Los Angeles Rams: Flashes of a Super Bowl powerhouse still surface, but key injuries and a merciless opening slate are already threatening to derail L.A.'s all-in campaign.

San Francisco 49ers: Stacking wins through another wave of injuries is more than just resilience—it's a reminder that a healthy version of this roster just might be the Super Bowl favorite.

Seattle Seahawks: Surviving self-inflicted wounds carried them to a ring, but an ugly stumble against Washington served notice that those bad habits will very likely derail a repeat bid.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy Address Viral Video of Heated Exchange in Steelers' Loss to Browns
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy says he regrets his heated exchange with quarterback Aaron Rodgers in the first quarter of Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy says he regrets his heated exchange with quarterback Aaron Rodgers in the first quarter of Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns.

"What's said on the field, the way I grew up in this game, usually stays on the field. That's not the case today. I understand that," McCarthy said after the game. "Any negative communication on my part, I wish I wouldn't use those words."

The incident took place when the game was still scoreless in the first quarter as Rodgers yelled toward the sideline while apparently waiting for a play call on 1st and 10.

Rodgers said after the game the noise at Huntington Bank Stadium had impacted his ability to communicate with his coaches.

"It was loud," Rodgers said. "So some of the calls, it was hard to hear, for sure."

The Steelers dropped to 2-2, which allowed the Browns (3-1) to climb to the top of the AFC North ahead of Sunday's slate.

McCarthy wasn't the only person Rodgers seemed frustrated with during Thursday night's loss.

The NFL on Prime broadcast also showed a video of Rodgers sharing a heated exchange with his wide receivers.

The opening drive on which McCarthy and Rodgers had their confrontation ultimately ended in a touchdown, although it took 17 plays and almost 10 minutes on the field.

"First drive was hectic... I was talking faster than normal," McCarthy said . "I think once we settled in after that drive, which resulted in a touchdown, I thought the communication was solid."

The Steelers had less success on offense following that opening score. Rodgers threw an interception on the next possession, and the next drive to get into scoring range ended with a missed field goal.

Rodgers found Pat Freiermuth in the end zone and converted a two-point try with less than two minutes remaining to pull the Steelers back even, but the Browns pulled ahead on their final drive thanks to a 56-yard field goal from Andre Szmyt.

An attempt at a Hail Mary from Rodgers to Roman Wilson was intercepted to seal the Browns' win.

The Steelers were ultimately outgained 372-361 as Rodgers finished the game 22-of-40 for 299 passing yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions.

Rodgers said ahead of the Week 4 matchup he felt his team's offense had started from zero this offseason, but there are "some vibes that start to flow a little bit if you put together a couple good performances in a row" (h/t Steelers.com's Mike Prisuta ).

The Steelers have so far been unable to accomplish that by putting together consecutive wins. They'll look to get back in the win column in Week 5 against the Indianapolis Colts.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson Praises 'Electric' Browns Fans After Beating Steelers to Take AFC North Lead
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has changed his stance on the crowd at Huntington Bank Field since accusing fans this preseason of rooting against him.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has changed his stance on the crowd at Huntington Bank Field since accusing fans this preseason of rooting against him.

Watson praised the home crowd as "electric" following a 27-24 Thursday night win over the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers.

"It was electric. It was amazing... from start to finish, the crowd was in it," Watson said after the win (h/t 92.3 The Fan). "The energy of the stadium, we fed off them."

Report Card Grades for the Browns' Big Win 📝

Watson led the Browns on a game-winning drive that will allow Cleveland to head into the weekend as the top team in the AFC North.

Browns head coach Todd Monken said after the win his team is finally in a position "our fans want to be in."

The Steelers pulled ahead by two points with less than two minutes left in regulation Thursday night.

Watson connected with Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin and K.C. Concepcion on his way to getting his team within range for a game-winning 56-yard field goal from Andre Szmyt.

It marked the third straight game in which Watson led his team on a game-winning drive.

Watson connected with Blake Whiteheart on a 17-yard touchdown pass with just under four minutes remaining in a 23-19 Week 2 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

He found Fannin in the end zone with less than two minutes left in a 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers last Sunday.

Watson is the first Browns quarterback since Brian Snipe to lead game-winning drives in the fourth quarter or later in three straight games, per ESPN Research (h/t Daniel Oyefusi ).

He had recorded just a single game-winning drive since 2020 prior to making his comeback this season, per the AP's Josh Dubow .

Watson and the Browns will be on the road for Week 5 against the New York Jets before hosting Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens for another big AFC North showdown in Week 6.

articles.title: Al Michaels glosses over Deshaun Watson's two dozen sexual misconduct lawsuits, calls them a 'thing'
articles.summary: Al Michaels dismissed Deshaun Watson's sexual misconduct allegations as a "thing" during the Cleveland Browns and Steelers primetime matchup.
articles.body: The Deshaun Watson story isn't fully written because this Cleveland Browns season isn't over and neither is his career. But Amazon Prime play-by-play announcer Al Michaels figures he can tell the tale without mentioning the most important and disgusting parts: The sexual misconduct and abuse allegations, and the dozen lawsuits Watson settled afterward to keep his career afloat. The Browns and the Pittsburgh Steelers were on Thursday Night Football this week and that, of course, put Watson in the spotlight. Some would want him put in crosshairs, given his history with the 27 women who filed civil lawsuits against Watson alleging sexual misconduct and assault, mostly during massage appointments between 2017 and 2020 while he was with the Houston Texans. DESHAUN WATSON GOES FROM CLEVELAND VILLAIN TO HERO IN BROWNS UPSET WIN, AS HOME CROWD TURNS JEERS TO CHEERS Those allegations were the primary reason the Texans sat Watson the entire 2021 season and traded him to the Browns in 2022. Those allegations and Watson settling all the lawsuits were the reason the NFL suspended him for 11 games his first season in Cleveland. But Michaels expects NFL fans to know these details. And he cannot be bothered with mentioning any of them even when discussing Watson's history. "If you follow football, you know the story," Michael said. "We don't have to go through the whole Deshaun Watson thing." BROWNS PICK DESHAUN WATSON AS THEIR STARTING QB DESPITE HOME CROWD BOOING AND HIS '17 AWAY GAMES' COMMENTS We don't. But you should go through some of it because you brought it up, Al. You started the discussion about Watson's history and how it has affected his relationship with Browns fans. "It's great, all of a sudden he's got these issues," Michaels said. "We all know what they were. They make the trade for him. It looks like a terrible trade. He's hurt. Hasn't played that much. Can he win the fan base over?" So, Michaels mentions a terrible trade, suggesting the Browns overpaid. Check. He mentions Watson's injuries. Check And he asks if Watson can win fans over as if the only stuff they have to get over are the facts their team paid a steep price, he's been injured, and hasn't played well when healthy. DESHAUN WATSON HARBORS NO ILL WILL TOWARD CLEVELAND AFTER COLLECTING $184M FOR 19 TDS IN FOUR SEASONS But the part about allegedly forcing some of those massage therapists to fondle him against their will, or the NFL successfully proving Watson committed "sexual assault" against multiple massage therapists is something about which football fans should be fully versed, according to Michaels. Look, the point here is not to demand that every mention of Watson's name be followed by a comprehensive detailing of his misconduct history. But when deciding to explain his history and his relationship with the Browns' fan base – which at varying times over the years has booed him and flooded radio call-in shows complaining about his alleged misdeeds, settled lawsuits, and suspension – then it behooves Michael to provide that context. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! And Michaels didn't merely skip the full story but seemingly minimized the allegations of assault. He called it all a "thing." He said it's not necessary to mention otherwise. This "thing" probably hasn't been forgotten by Watson's victims. Whatever you think of their stories, profession, anything else, the sheer number of women who shared their similar experiences with the quarterback is hard to dismiss. Except if you're Al Michaels.
